# Penmoss decision log

This is the durable record of every product, architecture and working decision for Penmoss. Agents and people read it before starting work.

- **Product decisions (D-series)** were made with Ryan: in the interview on 21 Oct 2026 and in follow-up questions on 22 Oct 2026. When a decision changes, add a new row and mark the superseded row; never rewrite history.
- **Architecture decisions (A-series)** came from the independent review of the plan on 21 Oct 2026. [`architecture.md`](architecture.md) describes the system as it is now.
- **Working agreements (W-series)** govern how agents do the work.
- Longer write-ups go in [`docs/adr/`](adr/). Link them from here.

| D31 | CRDT is Yjs 14: `@y/y` 14.0.0-rc.29 and `@y/prosemirror` 2.0.0-15, pinned exactly and wired into TipTap directly, with a guard that stops editor plugins repairing content the binding renders. The NoteDoc Durable Object is a thin Yjs-protocol handler on hibernatable WebSockets, not y-partyserver                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | The T4 spike measured both stacks ([ADR 0003](adr/0003-crdt-yjs-version.md)). Yjs 14 met all three D16 conditions: TipTap edits and undo, offline merge on the Durable Object, attribution. Yjs 13 also passed, but its editor views diverged when concurrent deletes emptied a callout. Exact pins, the engine-agnostic sync layer and the T4 test suites contain the release-candidate risk. y-partyserver needs Yjs 13 and saves on a debounce. Ryan reviews the result at Checkpoint A. |

| D34 | **Every action works in every client, period (24 Oct 2026, Ryan's feedback on the Mac app, #80).** Nothing is browser-only: Delete for good, Devices, agent tokens, the recovery code, Status and approving another sign-in work in the Mac app and, through T40's slices, on Android. Native clients guard each destructive or admin change with the OS's own check: Touch ID or the Mac's password on the Mac, never a plain confirmation; BiometricPrompt or the screen lock on Android. In-app confirmations stay. Amends A15 and A223 for native apps; the model is A503 and A504.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| D35 | **Agents can do nearly everything Ryan can, and none of it is permanent (25 Oct 2026, Ryan, #104).** A read-and-write agent token trashes and restores notes, manages folders, saves, restores and reverts versions, attaches files, changes settings and renames tags, each under its name. Its note changes revert in History, what it deletes waits in Trash, and Agent activity undoes the rest. No admin scope; nothing deleted for good. A folder-scoped token acts only inside its folder, never workspace-wide. Amends A133, A218, A410, A440; rules A560–A562, A564–A569.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Ryan on the review: "make it undoable. Nothing an agent does should be permanent." Daily limits (A562) keep a looping or misled agent from outrunning his notice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| D66 | **The roadmap moves to Linear (Ryan, 8 Nov 2026; supersedes W8, amends D41 and W13).** Open work lives in Linear's **Penmoss** team (`PEN`) in the Redhale workspace, not in GitHub issues and Project 8. Then an agent fixed them up through the Linear MCP: statuses, labels merged into the workspace's Feature, Bug, Improvement and Chore, a Blocked label, estimates from `size-*`, blocked-by relations and the PEN references. Multi-PR work is a Linear project: Software factory, Public release, Search by meaning. Done and Removed issues stay on GitHub. GitHub issues on `htxryan/penmoss` stay the public way in, for people outside and for Send feedback: the `Linear intake` workflow (`.github/workflows/linear-intake.yml`) copies each new one into PEN Triage through Linear's API, one way, with a link back. Linear's own GitHub issue sync is not used: it is two-way only, and would copy PEN issues into the public repository. The migrated GitHub copies move to `htxryan/penmoss-private`, closed, each pointing to its PEN issue, so the public tracker starts empty. Project 8 is closed, not deleted. Pull requests say `Fixes PEN-<n>`. The software factory still reads Project 8 and is stopped until its own plan moves it to Linear. Migration plan: [Penmoss to Linear](https://claude.ai/artifact/1GNAiBPpfggHNNnU2xDdsW), tracked as PEN-1. |

## Architecture decisions

| ID    | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Detail in plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A1    | **Durable Objects are the source of truth.** Each note's Yjs document lives in a `NoteDoc` Durable Object. The folder tree, ordering, note registry, assigned git paths and per-user settings live in a `WorkspaceDoc` Durable Object. D1 and Vectorize are rebuildable indexes behind one query interface. The auth tables are the only canonical data in D1, and they are exported to R2 nightly.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `#architecture`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| A2    | **Cloudflare Access protects only `app.penmoss.app`.** `api.penmoss.app` (`/api`, `/sync`, `/mcp`) is checked by the Worker, which accepts an Access JWT or a scoped, hashed, revocable bearer token, and returns a 401 JSON error, never a login redirect. The CLI signs in with a device code; Electron and Android get their token through a deep link or loopback callback.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | T5                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A3    | **Attribution.** Each device and agent writes under its own Yjs client ID, which a Durable Object table maps to an actor. Versions are stored as full state copies. Reverting an agent edit is a three-way merge (before, after, current) that reports overlapping changes as conflicts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | T4, T21, T24                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A4    | **Daily notes merge across offline devices.** The note ID comes from the date. The template insert is built only from the date and the template, under client IDs derived from hashes of the updates it produces (built once under a fixed ID; identity and title apart from the body), so builds whose output differs never share an ID and clocks, and the title is never doubled (A76). If the two devices' updates can't be made byte-identical, the fallback is for the server to insert the template.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | T19                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| A5    | **Restores can't duplicate content.** Every document has an epoch. A client whose epoch doesn't match the server's saves its unsynced changes as a conflict copy instead of merging them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | T8, T31                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| A6    | **Folder cycles are resolved when the tree is read.** A deterministic rule breaks a cycle created by concurrent moves; nothing writes a revert.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | T7                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A7    | **Local storage.** Each client keeps one IndexedDB store keyed by note ID, holding the merged update, state vector and plain text (not y-indexeddb). A service worker serves the app shell offline.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | T4, T8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| A8    | **Change events are debounced and sequenced.** A Durable Object alarm debounces events (about 2 s after the last change; see A19) and stamps each with a monotonic sequence number. Consumers read current state and make idempotent upserts guarded by that sequence number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | T6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A9    | **One schema everywhere.** The ProseMirror schema and the markdown codec live in `packages/core`. TipTap extensions are built from the core specs, and CI checks that the two schemas are equal. | A19   | **Index scheduling and batch limits (Phase 1 review).** The index alarm is a trailing debounce: it fires 2 s after the latest change, but no more than 30 s after the first unindexed one, so a typing session costs a few queue messages rather than one every 2 s (D20 quotas). Every change re-arms the alarm. A failed queue send keeps the change pending and re-arms the alarm with backoff (5 s doubling to 5 min) instead of relying on the runtime's limited alarm retries. A message handler error closes the socket with 1011, so a dropped update is never followed by a step-2 reply. `/sync/batch` decodes and encodes base64 inside each NoteDoc, reports a failing note in its own `error`, and marks notes past 8 MB of reply as `deferred` for the client to request again. A read-only or update-less batch entry never creates a note; an unknown note answers with a null epoch. A stale index message doesn't bump the workspace clock. | A20   | **Offline replica (T8).** Tabs share the IndexedDB store safely by merging inside the write transaction: each record carries a `rev`, and a writer that finds another tab's `rev` merges instead of overwriting, then pulls the other tab's changes into its open editor (no Web Locks or BroadcastChannel). The client holds back its sync reply until the session's epoch is checked. A mismatch saves unsynced work as a " (conflict copy)" note with a new id and fresh Yjs items, then reopens on the server's epoch. `/sync/batch` takes the client's `epoch` and applies nothing when it differs. Refusals stop the provider instead of retrying: 401/403/409, 1008, 1002/1003/1007 and an engine mismatch. After a refused upgrade, the client asks over HTTP for the reason, because browsers hide it. 1011 and dropped connections reconnect with `unsynced` kept. Catch-up runs on start, reconnect, session change, focus, every 30 s and after closing an unconfirmed note. It skips open notes and advances its clock only after every changed note has been fetched. IndexedDB v2 adds a `state` store for the clock. The service worker serves pages network-first, falls back to the cached shell, and never touches `/api`, `/sync` or `/auth`. One sync pill in the sidebar covers all notes. The workspace document uses the same handshake, but only stops on an epoch change until restores exist (T31). Review follow-ups: a restore is adopted inside one IndexedDB transaction that also writes the conflict copy, built from the record as stored then; a record that already has the server's epoch is left alone, so tabs make one copy between them. A note closed while a restore is adopted keeps edits that never reached the store as a conflict copy (`destroy()` reports `{ discarded, unsavedLocal }`). `/sync/batch` answers `Gone` for a note the client synced before but the server no longer has: unsynced changes become a conflict copy uploaded as a new note, and the original is marked deleted and synced. It answers `Read-only` for a read-only token's upload, which stays unsynced. A note whose upload alone gets a 413 is downloaded without it and stays unsynced. IndexedDB v3 adds a `meta` store kept in step with every write, so the note list never reads update blobs, and the stored clock only moves forward. Request budget: catch-up skips hidden tabs, runs in one tab at a time (Web Locks `penmoss-catchup`; the others refresh their list after it), leaves at least 5 s between passes (focus and visibilitychange collapse into one), and skips notes open in any tab (each holds a shared `penmoss-note:<id>` lock). The workspace shares the notes' IndexedDB connection and version-change handling, and its stops show in the pill as "Folders: …"; it files unregistered notes only while its socket is live and synced. The service worker falls back to the cached shell after 3 s without a network answer, and keeps the previous shell cache for pages still running the old build.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Shiki's TextMate grammars are more accurate, which matters less in notes than size. Formulas are core's `inlineMath`/`blockMath` atoms: `$…$` and `$$` + Enter create them; clicking a formula (or Enter on a selected one) edits its LaTeX in a field, and a block formula previews while edited. The field remembers the LaTeX it opened with: closing it unchanged writes nothing, so a peer's concurrent edit stands; changed on both sides keeps the peer's version and offers ours ("Use mine" / "Keep theirs"); closing the editor (switching notes) saves it first; a formula a peer deletes mid-edit comes back with the typed LaTeX. | A31   | **Attachment uploads within the Free-plan CPU limit (T10, D20).** The Worker never hashes an upload. It writes the first 64 bytes it read to check the type, releases the locks and pipes the rest of the body natively (`body.pipeTo`) to R2 with the expected SHA-256 (`R2.put(…, { sha256 })`), so no per-chunk JavaScript runs. R2 checks the digest. Only R2's checksum refusal (error 10037, BadDigest) is 400 `hash_mismatch`; any other R2 failure is 503 `storage_unavailable`, which clients retry. Measured in Node with SHA instructions (`apps/server/perf/attachments-cpu.perf.ts`), SHA-256 costs about 0.4 ms of CPU for 1 MB, 2 ms for 5 MB, 10–15 ms for 20 MB and 27–31 ms for 50 MB, so hashing in the Worker would break the 10 ms limit for large photos. The route without hashing measures 0.4–1.8 ms up to 50 MB, and the perf test asserts under 5 ms at every size. Over 50 MB is 413 before the body is read, and a missing `Content-Length` is 411. Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and AVIF are accepted, judged by the file's magic number rather than its declared type. AVIF counts as a major or compatible brand, so MIAF `mif1` files pass and HEIC does not. SVG is refused because it can carry script. A hash already stored answers 200 without reading the body. `GET` answers 304 to a matching `If-None-Match`. Non-image attachments and the 20 MB git cut-off come with T13 and T27. Bytes sit apart so flag and LRU updates never rewrite a blob; v4 was reshaped before it shipped. The upgrade only adds stores and reuses the A20 blocked and versionchange handling. Adding an image writes the bytes and its upload record in one transaction. A hash already stored is stored once; adding it again before the server has it replaces the bytes and restarts a failed upload. One queue per tab uploads one image at a time while `navigator.onLine` is true. It retries with persisted, jittered backoff (2 s doubling to 5 min), which survives restarts, and retries at once when the network or a session returns. A network error ends the pass. On 400 `hash_mismatch` the local bytes are re-hashed: intact bytes retry, damaged ones fail. Other 400s and 411, 413 and 415 mark the file failed (kept locally, not retried). Failed uploads never count as synced: the pill shows `N images failed` with a Retry action. Tabs do not coordinate: a duplicate upload is a cheap 200. The pill's `pending` counts notes plus images waiting to upload. Object URLs are shared per image and reference-counted by the node views, and the last release revokes them. A view waits and retries for a missing image until it closes; a lookup without a signal tries once. Downloaded images are evicted least recently shown first above 256 MB; images added on the device, not yet uploaded, or on screen are never evicted. First, a `<` at the end of a text run is escaped only when `<local@domain>` would really complete across the following spans (``<`@a>` ``, `<x*y*@a.b>`). Ordinary prose such as ``List<`T` `` or `a<*x*` is unchanged. Second, the whole run of `=` beside a highlight delimiter is escaped. Rule 14 of `markdown-normalisation.md` and the `link-definition-guard` and `angle-brackets-before-spans` fixtures pin these. | A40   | **Slash menu and markdown shortcuts (T14).** TipTap's Suggestion 3.32.0 (plain ProseMirror, no Yjs internals) tracks the `/query` and positions the menu with Floating UI 1.8.0. The editor package renders it, the toolbar and the drag handle as plain DOM, not React, so the editor stays framework-free for Electron and the Android WebView (the plan's `.tsx` file names became `.ts`). Only a `/` the user just typed opens the menu (a flag set in `handleTextInput`, cleared after the next transaction), at the start of a line or after a space, and never in a code block or inline code (marks at the caret or stored). A click, an arrow, an undo or a paste that leaves the caret after an existing `/word` does not open it, so Enter or Tab there keep their usual meaning; an open menu follows its query through a paste. Commands write through `execCommand('copy')` inside the gesture (no permission prompt), falling back to the async Clipboard API; a "Copied as …" status confirms them. A setting changed before the local copy was read, or before this session's first sync brought the server's state (a new device, or one that was offline), was concurrent with the stored value it replaced, so about half the time that value won, and the change vanished at once or on the next reload. The workspace writes the change at once and remembers it until the first sync; after the local copy is read and again after that sync, any such setting a stored value won over is written again, now after that value, so it wins on every device (removing a setting too: before the value arrived, removing it removed nothing). | A93   | **Escapes are checked against the markdown as written (codec fuzzing).** The serialiser chose escapes for `==` and `<` from the raw text, but to-markdown then writes some characters differently, so a few notes did not round-trip. A `==` after an escaped character (``==a\`== b==``, and likewise after `~`, `*`, `_`, `[` or `$`), or after whitespace written as a reference (`&#x20;`, `&#xA;`), could close or open a highlight. Escaping one `=` of a longer run left a bare `==` beside it (`a\=== b`). And `<~@a>` lost the escape on its `<`, as did a `<` in link text that an autolink could join across spans (`[*<*@a>](url)`). A last pass over each written text run now escapes the first `=` of any bare `==` that can still open or close, and any `<` that still starts an email autolink; link text is checked for autolinks across its spans like other text. Text that already round-tripped can gain one `\` when next saved (`a~== b` becomes `a~\== b`); it parses to the same document. | A120  | **The agent edit engine (T24, A3).** Agents edit through operations, never by sending Yjs updates or whole documents: create, append, insert under a heading, replace a section, find-and-replace, set properties, move and tag. The NoteDoc plans each one against the note as it is at that moment and applies it as the smallest change: the target body is built from the live top-level blocks (blocks the operation does not touch are the live blocks themselves; a block the agent sent back unchanged is swapped for the live one by its markdown, `reuseBlocks` in `@penmoss/core/diff-apply`, generalised from A81), turned into a Yjs delta and diffed into the body (`setBody`, A80). Only what the operation changed gets new Yjs items, so a human typing in another block at the same moment loses nothing, and wikilink note ids, embeds, table column widths and inline tags in untouched blocks survive. The edit runs in one transaction under a fresh client id mapped to the agent's actor (A3); pending changes are versioned first (A79), and the edit becomes a version of its own (reason `edit`, summary naming the operation, e.g. `Replaced section “Plans” · +3 −1 lines`; an agent's quick run of edits shares one, A131), which Revert undoes by three-way merge (A81). Markdown is parsed and diffed in the Durable Object, never in the Worker (D20). | A121  | **Base versions (T24).** `GET /api/notes/:id/content` returns the note's markdown, body, headings and `baseVersion`: the id of a version holding exactly that content, or of a hidden read checkpoint while changes are outside any version (A130; reads never version). Every edit accepts a `baseVersion` (required to replace a section or text, A128) and answers with the version it produced and its id as `baseVersion`, the next edit's base. The check is about what the operation targets, not the whole note: the section (heading and blocks) for section edits and appends under a heading, the whole lines around every match for find-and-replace, the title or frontmatter tags being set. If the target differs between the base and now, the edit fails with 409 `conflict` and `details` (`target`, `base`, `current`, each cut at 4,000 characters, A138); a base no longer in the history (or an expired checkpoint) gives 409 `base_unknown`. Appending to the end, tagging and moving have no target that can go stale. | A122  | **How operations address a note (T24).** A heading is matched by its text as shown (a wikilink by its label), case-insensitively, with an optional level (`## Plans`); two matches are 422 `heading_ambiguous` and none is 422 `heading_not_found`, each listing the note's headings. A section runs from its heading to the next heading of the same or a higher level, subsections included; `section` replaces the blocks under the heading (the heading stays) or inserts at their start (`prepend`) or end (`append`), and `append` with a heading adds at the section's end. Find-and-replace works on the body's markdown exactly as an agent reads it (links written with current titles), matching prose only unless `scope` is `markdown` (A137): the text must occur once (422 `text_not_found` or `text_ambiguous`) unless `all` is set, and only the result is parsed. Frontmatter is accepted only when creating a note, and only `title` and `tags`; afterwards `properties` sets the title and the frontmatter tags (the only frontmatter the document holds, A16, A73). Any other key is refused, 422 `unknown_properties`, on create and in `properties` alike (A136). A note in Trash refuses edits (409 `in_trash`) except a tag rename. | A125  | **Tag rename and merge run on the server (T24, supersedes A74's online path).** Online, the app sends `POST /api/tags/rename` with `from`, `to` and the ids of the notes it holds with the tag (Trash included). The WorkspaceDoc stores a job with those notes plus the ones the D1 tag index lists, answers 202 with the list, and works through it from its alarm, 25 notes per run, each renamed by its own NoteDoc through the engine (`renameTagInDoc`, one version per note, attributed to whoever asked; notes in Trash too). Each step is idempotent, a failed note is retried after 30 s and given up on (logged) after 5 attempts, the alarm is re-armed whatever a run does, and jobs run one at a time, so a crash or redeploy resumes where it stopped (A132). A rename also covers the notes of waiting or recent renames into its source tag (A132). Devices only, at most 5 waiting renames and 2,000 notes each (A133). | A157  | **Raw markdown opens in the editor; mixed lists are lists (T25 review, amends A9).** Cause of notes that would not open: for markdown the model has no node for (a list mixing `- [ ]` and `- ` items, HTML, `<br>`, footnotes), the codec keeps a `rawMarkdown` block or `rawInline` span, and since T24 agents' markdown reached notes through the engine; the editor's schema had neither node, so `@y/prosemirror` threw `node type does not exist in the schema` on open and the app showed an error over an empty body (also a daily note from a template holding such markdown). The codec maps what agents write most: a bullet list mixing task and plain items becomes adjacent task and bullet lists, one per run, at any depth, each with its own looseness, written apart with alternating bullets (`-`, `*`); a `<br>` between text in a paragraph is a hard break, the spaces beside it dropped. The serialiser writes a paragraph of only spaces as an empty one (it wrote a task item's `[ ]` on its own line). Pastes never make raw nodes: pasted markdown's raw parts stay text, as before, so pasted HTML never reaches a note's markdown live. Production (3 notes, no agent tokens issued) can hold raw nodes only from a template or a revert; any that do now open, as raw blocks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| A212  | **Folder names are assigned once; every path fits a Windows clone; names fold case as filesystems do (T27 review, amends A201).** The GitMirror stores each folder's name (`folders`: parent, sanitised name, name) and keeps it while the folder's own name and parent stay, so deleting one "Work" never renames the other "Work (ID)", and moving the older one next to a namesake gives it the suffix instead of the one already there; new, renamed and moved folders are named after the kept ones, by id, with a suffix where a sibling or a hand-made file (A217) has the name. Paths stay within 200 UTF-16 units (Windows' 260 less 60 for the clone's own folder): note names are cut to 80 characters before a suffix (at most 112 with suffix and `.md`), folder names to 56 and folder paths to 87; a cut folder name ends in `~` and six characters of a hash of its id, and a folder whose parent's path leaves no room is placed at the top under such a name. Names compare by `nameKey`: NFC, upper then lower case, NFC again, which folds final sigma and decomposed letters as APFS and NTFS do (and `ß` with `ss`, which only costs a suffix). The Obsidian check flags long paths and folds case the same way. | A213  | **An attachment upload fits a Durable Object's memory, and one that does not cannot wedge the mirror (T27 review, amends A10, A210).** Measured with `apps/server/scripts/mirror-upload-memory.ts` (Node 24, the same V8; live heap plus ArrayBuffers with the references the code holds, each case in a fresh process): the old pipeline held 6.0 times the file, 120 MB for a 20 MB file against the 128 MB limit. The request body is now built straight into bytes (`blobRequestBody`: base64 in 24 KB steps; no binary, base64 or JSON string and no UTF-8 copy) and the blob SHA-1 streams through `DigestStream`: 2.33 times the file, 23.3 MB live for a file at the new 10 MB cap (27.0 MB allocated, garbage included); a copy of the body by the runtime would add 13.3 MB. Files over 10 MB stay out of git (was 20 MB). Before reading the bytes the mirror writes an attempt row (`upload_attempts`) and waits for `storage.sync()`; the row goes when the upload ends or fails with an error the run records. A row still there when the file is next uploaded means the object was reset meanwhile (an out-of-memory reset skips every `catch`); at 3 the file is skipped with that reason, so one file can stop at most three runs. Settings → Git mirror lists skipped files (too large, or crashed) and why; the notes keep their links as written. A file no written or waiting note uses any more stops waiting, and one uploaded in the run that drops it is not committed. Settings counts the files no device has uploaded yet. | A223  | ~~**Mac sign-in, sign-out and the device token (T29, A15; review round).**~~ _Superseded by D49 (T59)._ The app opens `/native-sign-in` in the default browser with a PKCE challenge and a one-time loopback redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`, opened for that sign-in only, ten-minute limit, `state` checked in constant time); after Approve it trades the code and verifier for a device token named “Mac app (<computer>)”. ~~**Native apps keep read-write tokens, never admin (A15; coordinator decision, 23 Oct 2026).**~~ _Superseded by D34 and A503–A504 (T41): the Mac app administers after Touch ID, and the browser-only screens below are gone._ The session carries the token's scopes (`/api/me`; an entry stored without them reads as read-write), and the page's `SessionManager.canAdminister` is false for it: admin-only commands and screens are hidden or replaced, never left to fail with a 403. Open in browser (`app.openInBrowser`) opens the same path on the app host; the main process accepts only a plain path there. Asking to sign in again cancels a pending sign-in (`AbortController`) and opens the browser afresh; a token that arrives for a cancelled sign-in is revoked. `DELETE /api/auth/token` signs the calling token out, with any scope and no id, so it can revoke nothing else; its device is signed out too when no live token is left on it. The app calls it before storing a new sign-in over an old token, and on Sign out (menu, palette and This Mac), which then forgets the token. Notes stay in the local replica after sign-out. The token lives only in the main process: encrypted with `safeStorage` (the Keychain) in `session.json` (0600), one entry per API origin, encrypted again when safeStorage reports a rotated key. Where encryption is unavailable it stays in memory only; on Linux the fixed-key `basic_text` backend counts as unavailable, and only an unpackaged test build may accept it (`PENMOSS_TEST_BASIC_TEXT_STORAGE=1`, for xvfb without a keyring). The page asks for the session over IPC (`NativeSessionSource`); its session store is in memory, never `localStorage`. A page's 401 forgets the stored token only if the server refuses that token (`/api/me`), since it may be for the token a new sign-in just replaced.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

| A260  | **The performance budgets are benchmarks in CI, never loosened (T31).** A `Performance budgets` job runs them apart from the smoke job: T22's search budgets (server FTS under 300 ms and the offline index under 150 ms on a seeded 5,000-note vault, and the D1 rows-read ceilings) and, in Playwright on the production build (`budgets.spec.ts`, `@budget`), typing p95 under 16 ms in a 10,000-word note and a note switch under 150 ms. Typing latency is the main thread's cost of a keystroke: from the keydown's `timeStamp` (so a busy thread counts) until every listener, ProseMirror's DOM observer, the Yjs binding and React's synchronous updates have run and style and layout are forced; the wait for the next frame is left out, because a task posted after a key event runs after the frame and would measure vsync (traced), which makes 16 ms meaningless. A note switch runs from the click's `timeStamp` until the note view is ready with the target's title and text, layout forced. Robustness on shared runners comes from measuring, not from slack: 60 warm-up keys, then three runs of 150 keys (letters, Backspace, Enter, no faster than one per 40 ms) and the median of the three p95s is asserted; switches get two warm-up round trips, then 8 per direction, the median per direction asserted and p95 logged. Headroom measured on the shared 4-CPU worker: typing p95 5–11 ms (2–3×), switch to the long note 52–60 ms (2.5×). **Finding:** on GitHub's runner (PR #64) typing p95 is 9.7 ms, but the switch to the 10,000-word note has a median of 137 ms (p95 282 ms), barely inside 150 ms; the switch to a short note is 31 ms. The cost is opening a long note (decoding its Yjs state and building and laying out the ProseMirror document): if the job starts failing, make that open cheaper (render the first screen first, or keep recently opened notes' views); never raise the budget. A failing budget is a finding to fix in the code, not a number to change. Typing cost today is about 2 ms of ProseMirror and Yjs and 2 ms of React (the note list re-sorts on every keystroke's `updatedAt`): the first lever if it regresses. The fps budgets (`@perf`) stay local, as before.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | T31                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

A dmg's name records its build, and every release `build-k` holds the dmg with the highest `n <= k`: a new release carries the newest earlier Mac app (its notes name the build), and a Mac app passes on to newer releases holding an older one, so Latest always has one and a late build never replaces a newer one. `.github/scripts/releases.mjs` restores that rule and Latest after every change, so the jobs may finish in any order; they share the `releases` concurrency group. CI builds have no update feed. A dispatch publishes nothing (A405); its dmg is the run's artifact. Known limit: a concurrency group holds one job running and one waiting, so a release job that arrives while one waits cancels the waiting one, and that build's APK or dmg is skipped (the next build's are not; A405 says how to re-run it).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

The budgets hold with more room on the Mac, thresholds unchanged (typing p95 7.2 ms against 10.1, budget 16; opening the long note 46 ms against 94, budget 150). | A405  | **The Mac release, hardened after the review of #79 (24 Oct; amends A403; amended by A1189: `mac-signing` and `android-sideload` also serve release.yml on `v*` tags, once Ryan allows them).** The `mac-release` job also needs `desktop` and publishes only once the Mac app's tests passed in the same run. A dispatch publishes nothing, even on main: its run number is not the build's, so the dmg's name and the app's `CFBundleVersion` would disagree; to redo a build's Mac app, re-run its push run's failed or cancelled jobs (same run number). The `pull_request` exclusion is not what protects the Mac: any push to the repository can run code on it, because a branch's own workflow file is what runs, for any event. The mitigation is the dedicated non-admin macOS account the runners run as, `penmoss-ci` (A404, `docs/ci.md`). Every action is pinned to a commit SHA, and checkouts use `persist-credentials: false`. Main-only secrets live in environments limited to `main` by a deployment branch policy, never in repository secrets (any branch's workflow can read those). The `android` job names `android-sideload` (the sideload keystore and password, A400) on pushes to main only, so a pull request's job never receives them; once a main run proves it, the repository-level copies are deleted. The `mac` job names `mac-signing` the same way, but it stays empty: each runner's folder belongs to the account its jobs run as, so any job can leave something in a runner that later reads main's secrets. **No signing secret goes into `mac-signing` while signing runs on these self-hosted runners**; Ryan is choosing between root-owned runner folders, a separate signed-release path and signing by hand (`docs/desktop.md` §3, `docs/ci.md` §7). Known limits: a release job runs for minutes, not seconds (`publish-apk` carries the 121 MB dmg into the new release), so close merges can cancel a waiting one; re-run it in its push run within 7 days, while its artifact is kept. A self-hosted job waits at most 24 hours for a runner, then fails (main shows red after a trip away), and GitHub removes a runner offline for 14 days. The Mac runners' caches (pnpm store, Electron, Gradle) serve branches' jobs and main's dmg build alike, so a branch's job could leave something there that a later release dmg uses.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
