| A410  | **The settings channel for a client that never reads Yjs (T40 P1a, ST2).** `/sync/tree` gains `settings`: the caller's values for `theme.id`, `theme.mode`, `timeZone`, `template.daily`, `template.weekly`, `capture.destination` and `note.fullWidth`, plus every `theme.custom.*` (a parsed theme, or `{id, base, deleted: true}` for a deleted one), each checked with the web's own rules and part of the tree's hash, so a change on the web reaches the phone on its next pass. **`PUT /api/settings`** takes `{set: {key: value \| null}, base: {key: previous \| null}}`. A base is required for every key set, at most 20 keys a request. It runs the web's `setSetting` in the WorkspaceDoc, as one server edit. Its rules: a theme id must be built in or a custom theme the user has; mode is light, dark or system; a time zone is an IANA zone (`isTimeZone`); a template written is at most 10,000 characters (a limit the web did not have, far above a day's skeleton; a longer one already stored is still sent and compared as it is, so a phone change based on it is not refused and one made without knowing of it never overwrites it); capture is `daily` or `inbox`; full width is a boolean; null removes a key. An unknown key or a bad value is a 400 `invalid_setting` naming it, and a body over the 1 MiB request limit a 413 `too_large`, never a 500 the phone would retry. A key whose stored value is no longer its `base` is a 409 `setting_changed` naming every such key, and nothing in the request is written, so a change made on the web while the phone was offline wins, as A359 does for moves. A value already stored is a no-op, so a resent request is harmless. Only a device token (or a browser session) may write: an agent token gets 403 `insufficient_scope` even with `write` (invariant 8). Writes to `theme.custom.*` wait for the theme editor (P1b), keyboard keys for P9 (ST8). The Worker imports `@penmoss/ui`'s theme subpaths only (`theme/schema` is newly exported), never the DOM code in its index. Code and tests: `apps/server/src/do/settings.ts`, `WorkspaceDoc.changeSettings`, `routes/api.ts`; `apps/server/test/settings.test.ts`, the route probe in `folder-scope.test.ts`; contract `apps/android/contract/settings-v1.json` (with `templateMaxChars`, which the phone's `SettingLimits` must equal), checked by the server suite and the Kotlin `SettingsContractTest`. _Amended by A568 (T42): write-scope agent tokens read and change settings too; folder-scoped ones only read._                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| A411  | **Settings changed on the phone wait in Room and go first in each pass (T40 P1a, ST2; amended after the review of #90).** Room schema 6 adds `pending_settings`: one row per key, holding the latest value, the value the phone saw before its first change (the `base`), and the values sent for it without an answer yet (`sent`). Changing a key back to its base deletes the row, unless a value is out without an answer: the server may hold that one, so the row stays and puts the base back once it lands. What every screen and the editor page show is the last tree's settings with these rows laid over, so a change shows at once, offline too. Each pass sends them first (`PassWork.beforePass`), so the tree that pass reads already has them. A row changed again while its request was out is rebased on what was sent and goes in the same pass. A tree or a 409 that shows a value this phone sent without hearing back is its own change landing (a lost reply): the row is done, or rebased on it and sent on. A tree or a 409 showing any other value (changed elsewhere) drops the row, the newer choice winning. A 400, a 413 or a 403 drops the changes it names (all, when it names none) and Settings home says which and why until dismissed, never silently; offline, a 404 (a server not yet deployed) or a 5xx leaves them for the next pass. Pending settings count as unsent, so a background run sends them and sign-out keeps them and says so (A360). Before the server has sent settings (one without the channel) nothing can be changed, and the screens say why. The quick-capture destination stays one value. Once settings are known, picking the other destination in the capture sheet changes it through this queue, and the capture no longer carries `remember` (A346). A Settings choice also clears `remember` on captures still waiting from before. Either way, the later choice wins; the capture's own `remember` is kept only for a server without the channel. Templates are counted against the server's limit and cannot be saved over it. Code and tests: `NoteStore` (`changeSetting`, `settingsToSend`, `settingsSent`, `settingsOvertaken`, `settingsRefused`, `observeSettings`), `sync/SettingsSender.kt`, `capture/Captures.kt`; `SettingsStoreTest`, `SettingsSyncTest`, `SettingsScreensTest`, `AppBackgroundTest`, `MigrationTest`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| A412  | **The phone knows the built-in themes itself (T40 P1a, ST4).** `contract/themes-v1.json` holds the built-in themes, the token keys with their labels and groups, the fonts and the note width's range. The editor page's vitest generates it from `@penmoss/ui` (`PENMOSS_WRITE_CONTRACTS=1`) and fails when it differs, and `engine-bridge` bundles it as a resource. With it the theme grid draws each theme's miniature offline, and the phone resolves the chosen theme and mode itself (`ThemeCatalogue.resolve`, as `resolveThemeSettings` does) the moment Ryan picks one, before the server has it. A server without the settings channel still sends the resolved `appearance` (A305), which is used as before. Kotlin never guesses a colour and never validates a theme: the server does (A410). | A416  | **`PUT /api/settings` writes custom themes, merged with edits made elsewhere (T40 P1b, ST2, ST5; extends A410).** A `theme.custom.<id>` value is a theme or the deletion mark `{id, base, deleted: true}`, and its `base` is the theme as it was when the phone's edit began, or null for a new theme. The value must pass the web's `parseTheme` with no problems, and its id must match the key's. A 400 `invalid_setting` refuses a bad theme, an id that does not match, and a base that is not that theme. The server stores an edit as `storedTheme(theme, stored, base)`, the web's own three-way merge: only the fields the phone changed since its base are written over what is stored now, so another device's edits to other fields since then are kept, as are fields this build does not know (A20). An edit of a theme deleted since gets a 409 `setting_changed`, as does a new theme whose id is taken by a different theme. A theme already stored as sent is a no-op, so a resent request writes nothing. A deletion always goes, even over an edit made elsewhere since. After the review of #91: a deletion is stored as `{id, base, deleted: true}` and nothing else (a probe had stored about 500 KB of padding in one), and deleting a theme the user never had stores nothing. The phone may make at most 50 custom themes (`CUSTOM_THEMES_MAX`): a new one past that is a 400 `invalid_setting` naming its key; edits and deletions still go. The web, writing its Yjs directly, has no limit. Custom keys are planned before the others, so one request can make a theme and choose it with `theme.id`; choosing a theme deleted in the same request is a 400. Agent tokens still get 403 (invariant 10). | A427  | **The app reports its errors to Penmoss, without note content (T40 P2b, AC7; A263).** `ErrorReporter` sends to `POST /api/errors` with source `android`: uncaught exceptions (its handler is installed before the app's graph is built, and chains the previous one, so the app still stops), the editor page's `error` messages, sync passes that failed for a reason other than being offline or signed out (a server error or a reply it could not read), and background runs that gave up after their last try for such a reason, which they name. As the web's `reporter.ts`: once per error (its message and first stack frame), not again while one like it waits (from any process), at most 20 a run and 10 waiting. Reports wait in a file (`files/error-reports.json`, written at once through a temporary file and a rename), not Room, so a crash is recorded before the process dies; every sign-out and every clearing of the cache (another workspace signed in) empty it, so one workspace's reports never reach another. They go after the next pass, oldest first; the first that cannot go stops the rest, and one the server refuses outright (a 4xx other than 401 and 429) is dropped. **Never note content (review of #93):** a report is scrubbed when it is recorded, so the file only ever holds scrubbed text: every note title and folder name the phone holds (kept in memory from a Room flow; three characters or more, whole words, longest first) and any quoted text (curly or straight, escaped quotes inside, and a quote left open running to the end) become `‹name›`, and what follows `JSON input:` in a JSON error (the reply it could not read) is withheld; all before the text is cut to size. Stack frames and exception class names are left as they are. Until any names are known (nothing pulled yet, or the app just started), the free text is withheld: only the exception's kind, its class names and its frames are kept. Sending scrubs again with the names Room holds then, and sends nothing if they cannot be read. Found on the emulator: the app's JSON leaves defaults out, so a default `source` never reached the server; `source` is now always written (`StatusApiTest`). Code and tests: `report/ErrorReporter.kt`, `PenmossApp.kt` (`followNames`), `PassWork`, `SyncCoordinator` (`onFailure`, `lastFailure`), `BackgroundSync` (`gaveUp`), `NoteEditorController` (`onPageError`), `SessionManager` (`forget`); `ErrorReporterTest`, `PhoneQueueTest`, `SyncStatusTest`, `SessionManagerTest`, `BackgroundSyncTest`, `NoteEditorControllerTest`, `StatusApiTest`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

| A430  | **Trash on the phone goes through the server, held in Room until it agrees (T40 P3a, NT12, NT14; both reviews of #94).** The phone never sets a note's deleted flag in Yjs (A11): Move to Trash and Restore change Room at once, offline too, and wait in the note's row as `trashChange` (1 move asked, 5 in flight, 2 sent; 3 restore asked, 6 in flight, 4 sent; schema 7, with schema 8 adding the seqs, `trashTried` and `trashNotice`). `TrashSender` sends restores before the notes are exchanged, and moves to Trash after the filer, once none of the note's own stored edits wait and a move made here is filed (`trashesDue`), so the server records the folder this phone had it in, as the web records its own. Each request is marked in flight, and tried (`trashTried`), before it goes: Undo or Restore meanwhile queues a restore, and Move to Trash during a restore queues a move. Offline, a 5xx, a 404 that does not say the note is gone, or a pass stopped mid-request: it is queued again and stays tried, as the server may have applied it, so a later Undo, Restore or Move to Trash still queues the opposite request. Only a request never tried is cancelled; only an answer clears the flag. Both routes are idempotent, so the cost is one extra request. `/sync/changes` cannot undo a change under way (`updateMetadata` keeps `deleted` as asked). A sent change settles on the first row that agrees or comes from after it (its `seq` above the one the server answered); earlier rows are held. Only seqs are compared, never the phone's clock with the server's. 409 `restored_since` drops the move, lists the note again and says so once ("“X” was restored on another device, so it was left out of Trash."), the notice kept on the note's row so one met by a background pass is said when the app is next open. Only a 404 that says the note is gone (`note_not_found`, or an older server's `not_found` "No such note") drops the phone's copy, as a purge does (A310). Any other 404 waits: to a restore, as an error does; to a move to Trash, as a server from before A431, which answers its plain "404 Not Found" (the server's JSON catch-all is never reached), so moves wait and Trash and Sync and storage say why, with Restore as the way to keep a note. A restore files the note back in the folder the server returns, through the filing queue (A352), listed there at once when the phone knows that folder. Schema 8's migration clears the changes clock, so the next pass reads every index row again and fills each note's seq. Waiting changes count as unsent: Sync and storage lists them, a background run sends them, sign-out keeps them. Code and tests: `NoteStore.kt`, `Daos.kt`, `TrashSender.kt`, `PassWork.kt`; `TrashSyncTest`, `TrashStoreTest`, `MigrationTest`, `PhoneQueueTest`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| A431  | **`POST /api/notes/:id/trash` (T40 P3a, NT12; both reviews of #94).** Moves a note to Trash for a client that never edits its document itself. Write scope (403 `insufficient_scope` for a read-only token; an agent that may write may trash, not purge, A83); a folder-scoped token gets 404 for a note outside its folder, as on every `/api/notes/:id/*` route. The NoteDoc records the deletion as a device's own would, through `serverEdit` (open sockets see it at once): the flag, when, and the folder the tree had the note in (`setDeleted` with `at` and `folderId`). The content stays in the NoteDoc; D1 only indexes it. The WorkspaceDoc then takes the note out of the tree. Idempotent: a note already in Trash answers with its recorded time and folder and is unfiled again, which also finishes a deletion that left it in the tree (tested). `{ knownSeq? }` is the newest index seq (`seq` in `/sync/changes`) the caller had seen when it was asked: the NoteDoc keeps its last restore's seq and actor (`undeleted_seq`, `undeleted_by`), and refuses with 409 `restored_since` only a request that has not seen a restore made by someone else. The caller's own restores never refuse it, and no clock is compared, so a device's clock cannot change the outcome. A row at the restore's own seq may already show it (an index event sent before the restore, snapshotted after it): a caller that saw only that row is refused, which errs towards the restore, and its next move goes once a later row arrives. No body is no precondition; a body that is not a JSON object is 400. The reply is `{ folderId, deletedAt, seq }`: rows with a higher `seq` show the change. `/restore` now also answers `restored` (whether it was in Trash) and `seq`. Both routes answer a note the NoteDoc does not have with 404 `note_not_found` "No such note", a code of their own, so a client drops its copy only then and never on another 404. The web and the Mac move notes to Trash in the note's document, where a concurrent restore merges like any edit, so they need no precondition. It needs a deploy before a phone with P3a can trash. Tests: `trash-route.test.ts`, `folder-scope.test.ts`, `history.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| A503  | **Native apps administer, each change after the device's own check (T41, D34; amends A15 and A223).** The Mac app signed in through `/native-sign-in` (an explicit Approve in the owner's browser session, PKCE) gets `read`, `write` and `admin`. The Android app stays `read` and `write` until T40 P2 adds its BiometricPrompt check (the server grants admin only to `deviceKind` `mac`; the approval page says what each app will be able to do). CLI device codes and agent tokens never get admin, as before, and every token stays revocable in Settings → Devices. Core's `ADMIN_ACTIONS` names every admin change (purge, revoke a device or token, create a token, sign out everywhere, recovery code, approve a sign-in, Back up now, Clear errors, restore, reindex); `adminActionOf(method, path, body)` maps a request to one, and a server test fails if an admin route that changes something is not in the table. Denying a CLI's sign-in is not checked: it changes nothing anyone could use. The page's `SessionManager.api` asks the native app's check (`NativeSessionSource.confirmAdmin`) before sending any such request and fails closed: no check, or a refused one, sends nothing, and the page shows the app's own reason (“Not done: this Mac did not confirm it was you.”). Admin reads (lists) need no check. In-app confirmations stay in front of it. A Mac token from before T41 is read-write: admin screens show “sign in again” (`AdminSignIn`), never Open in browser, and a 403 says the same. **What the check guards against:** a person at an unlocked, signed-in device. It does not guard against code running in the Mac app's page: the admin token lives in the renderer (the preload hands the session to the page), so such code could send admin requests itself. That is the same exposure the browser's admin session already has. Moving admin requests into the main process, with the admin token out of the renderer, is [#85](https://github.com/htxryan/penmoss/issues/85) (_done: A540–A543_). Android (T40 P2) asks BiometricPrompt with `BIOMETRIC_STRONG or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` (the screen lock where no biometric is enrolled) in Kotlin before it sends the same requests; its page never holds a token.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | T41                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| A504  | **The Mac's check: Touch ID or the Mac's password, never a plain confirmation (T41, A503; review of #84).** The page asks over IPC (`penmoss:admin:confirm`, accepted only from the main window's app frame; _since #85 `penmoss:admin:request`, with words for each change, A541_) with an action id; the main process takes the words from `ADMIN_ACTIONS`, never from the page, and runs a small signed helper in the app, `Contents/Resources/auth/Penmoss` (`apps/desktop/native/penmoss-auth.swift`): LocalAuthentication's `evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication)`, which is Touch ID with the account's password as its fallback (after a Touch ID lockout, with the lid closed, or with no finger enrolled). macOS shows “Penmoss is trying to delete a note for good”. Main passes the reason as the one argument, with no shell, and trusts only the exit code: 0 confirmed; 1 refused (cancelled or failed); 2 unavailable (no Touch ID and no password); anything else, a helper that is missing or will not start, or one still open after 2 minutes (it is killed) refuses with a clear reason. There is never a weaker dialog. One check at a time: a second request while one is open is refused, so a page cannot queue prompts. **Built and shipped:** `scripts/build-auth-helper.mjs` compiles it with `xcrun swiftc` for arm64 and x86_64 (minimum macOS 12) and joins them with `lipo` into `dist/native/Penmoss`. electron-builder's `beforePack` hook runs it for every Mac package (a Mac build without it fails), `mac.extraResources` ships it, and the app's signing signs it with the app: ad hoc today, Developer ID once the secrets exist. `task desktop:build` on a Mac builds it for development too. Elsewhere (Linux, the CI's xvfb runs) there is no helper and every admin change is refused; the Playwright suite stands in for it with a script through `PENMOSS_TEST_AUTH_HELPER`, honoured only by unpackaged builds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | T41                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

| A462  | **The phone's offline index is Room FTS4 over text folded as the server's tokenizer folds it, ranked as the web's offline index ranks (T40 P6, FD4).** `note_texts` holds each note's title, body, tags and headings as they are, for marks, and a folded copy of each (`ftitle`, `fbody`, `ftags`, `fheadings`), the content of an FTS4 `note_text_fts` (external content; Room's triggers keep them together), with the note's word count. Android's FTS4 cannot use unicode61, the server's tokenizer, so Kotlin's `SearchFold` does its work first (review B1): every separator of unicode61's tables becomes a space and every other character folds as unicode61 folds it (case, diacritics, the tables' exceptions), from the same tables as core's `tokenize`; Kotlin's `SearchStem` then stems each word as core's `stemTerm` does (a line-by-line port; review R4), and FTS4's simple tokenizer cuts exactly at the spaces (Ryan’s finds ryan, foo—bar finds bar, éclair finds Éclair, gardens finds garden). FTS4's porter is not used: it kept only the first and last 3 bytes of a word with a digit and the first and last 10 of a word over 20 bytes, so 5551234567 and 555999567 were one word and a prefix of a SHA, a long word or a long CJK run missed. `contract/search-fold-v1.json` holds the tables, core's words for every character of the Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, punctuation and other blocks, and core's stems of 111 terms (digits, SHAs, long words, Cyrillic, CJK); the phone gives the same words and stems. A query's words, phrases and `title:` words are stemmed the same way; the last word while typing matches its stem or any word it begins. Queries are read as `parseQuery` reads them and folded the same way: words and quoted phrases ANDed, `prefix*`, the last word a prefix while typing (2 letters or more), `-word` and `-"phrase"` leaving notes out (a second match subtracted in Kotlin), `title:` as each word in the title column (FTS4 takes a column only before a bare term), nothing typed ever FTS syntax, at most 12 clauses. Ranking is `LocalSearchIndex`'s bm25 (A101, the server's order) from `matchinfo('pcx')`: per clause, its count weighted by column (title 10, body 1, tags 5, headings 4), its idf from how many live notes it matches, and the note's length against the average; ties by id. `contract/search-ranking-v1.json` holds core's ids and scores for 35 queries over 37 notes, and the phone gives the same to 1e-6 (review S6). Marks come from FTS4's `offsets()` mapped back to the original characters: the title highlighted, and core's 16-token snippet of the body, or of the headings when the body holds no match. Filters join `notes`: a folder's subtree from Room, a tag or one nested under it from `note_tags` (`substr`, as A467), `updatedAt` at or after. Notes the index has no text for yet are matched on title and first line, as before, after the indexed ones. A two-letter prefix over 5,000 notes takes about 13 ms in Robolectric.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

A new `textDue` column (schema 15, default true) marks a held note whose text the index lacks: fetched before the index existed, or changed on a pass that asked for none. Such notes are exchanged once more on the next prefetching pass, after unsent, stale and missing notes, within the pass's batch limit, so the first fill spreads over passes. The server's text is stored only when the phone holds no unsent edits of the note after the exchange (else it lacks them); an applied or restored reply with the hash alone settles it, as does an older server's applied reply with no text at all, so an older server is asked once per change, not every pass; any other reply (deferred, kept apart) leaves it due. The editor page reports the open note's text, headings and tags (`text { noteId, text, headings, tags }`, capped the same way) 3 s after typing here pauses and as the note closes or the app goes to the background, only after edits made here, so this phone's unsent words are found offline; the same text again writes nothing, and its hash goes with the next exchange. Storage is the vault's text again, at most 256 KB a note (and 64 KB of headings); signing out clears it with the cache, and a note deleted for good leaves it. | A488  | **Pictures from web addresses are fetched by the app on the page's own origin (T40 P8, ED13; keeps A293).** The page's CSP stays `img-src 'self' data: blob:`. It fetches `https` only, with no user info in the URL and no cookies, cache or token (its own OkHttp client). It reaches public addresses only: a DNS answer is filtered through a vetted `Dns`, an address written in the URL is checked without DNS, and each of at most five redirects is checked again (no loopback, private, link-local, carrier NAT, unique-local or reserved addresses; mapped, NAT64 and 6to4 IPv6 judged by their IPv4, and local-use NAT64 refused). OkHttp connects to any digits-and-dots host as an address, which the system reads in short, octal or decimal forms (`127.1`, `0177.0.0.1`, `2130706433`), so only a plain dotted quad or an IPv6 address is taken as an address and every other numeric host is refused (re-review PB1). It uses no proxy, which would resolve the name past these checks. The type is sniffed from the bytes, never the server's word, and must be a picture type the app shows. It takes at most 20 MB, in a 200 MB LRU disk cache that is cleared at sign-out, and is served `no-store`. It never throws (A312) and is limited to two fetches at a time, one per address. `http:` pictures show their alt text. A web picture still tells its host the note was opened, as on the web.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| A540  | ~~**The Mac app's page holds a read-write token; the admin token stays in the main process (#85; amends A503 and A223).**~~ _Superseded by D49 (T59)._ After a sign-in, and on the first launch of a session from before #85, the main process asks `POST /api/auth/page-token` with its admin token for a second device token on the same device, read and write only. Both tokens are kept encrypted together in `session.json` (A223). `penmoss:session:get` hands the page only the page token, with `adminInApp: true`, and `pageSession` never hands over a token that has admin. Edits keep the Mac's author, since it is the same device. The main process's own requests go through Chromium's network stack (`net.fetch`), so the Mac's proxy and certificates apply. **No page token yet and none to be had** (offline, or a server without the route): the page is told `pending` and opens offline, notes and all, with no sign-in banner (S2); the main process asks again (15 s, doubling to 5 min) and tells the page when it has one. When no page token can be made, the main process asks whether the server refuses its admin token: if it does (the Mac was signed out from elsewhere while the app was closed), the app signs out instead of staying offline (re-review of PR #100, R1). When the page reports a 401, the main process checks both tokens: a refused page token is replaced, and a refused admin token signs the Mac out. The page may ask for that check at will, so it runs at most every 10 s (N5), and the page shows nothing until it answers, so there is no “signed out” flash (N4). After Sign out everywhere else, which keeps the main process's token and revokes the page's, a new page token is made before the page is answered. Sign out, and a new sign-in replacing a session, sign the whole device out with the admin token (`DELETE /api/devices/<own id>`, R2), so a page token whose answer was lost goes too; without admin, or refused, they revoke both known tokens, the page's first, so the device goes with the last. Every request main makes with a token refuses redirects, and the sign-in uses `net.fetch` too. Making a page token asks no owner check: it grants less than the caller holds. A Mac signed in before T41 holds a read-write token and hands it over as before. | A560  | **A deleted folder goes to Trash, for everyone (T42 review B3; D35).** Ryan: "make it undoable. Nothing an agent does should be permanent." Deleting a folder still moves its notes up to its parent at once (no note was ever deleted), but the folder now waits in the workspace document's `folderTrash` map with its subfolders (names, parents, places and sort modes) and, for each note it held, the folder and place it had and where the delete moved it. This holds for people's deletes too: the apps call the same `deleteFolder`, one rule is simpler, and people gain an undo they lacked. Trash lists deleted folders above deleted notes, with what they held, where from, who deleted them (an agent by name, ✦) and days left. **Restore** (web and Mac; Android is a gap in the T40 parity matrix) recreates the folder and its subfolders where they were, at the top level when the folder it was in is gone (`parentGone`), and moves back each note still where the delete left it. A note moved or deleted since stays where it is and Restore says how many; edits to a note's content do not matter. Restoring twice changes nothing. A delete made through the server records who made it (`deletedBy`: label and kind), so Trash shows "by Claude Code ✦" or a device's name; a delete in the web or Mac app's own document is yours and names no one. `GET /api/trash` likewise gives each note's `deletedBy` (`{ label, kind }`): the NoteDoc records the actor whose change deleted the note, whatever the path (sync, the REST route, an agent), and tells the WorkspaceDoc from its index alarm, which keeps it in its own SQLite (`trash_actors`) for 31 days, so the list makes one call and D1 needs no column. Notes trashed before this have none. A581's recovery replays `folderTrash` with the tree, so a folder deleted or restored on a refused replica keeps or loses its Trash record as it should (re-review R2). One delete of a folder of about 8,000 notes or more would be an update of about 1 MB, near the WebSocket message limit; far beyond Ryan's folders. Records older than 30 days are hidden and dropped at the next folder delete, as notes are purged after 30 days (A83). Being in the Yjs document, it works offline and syncs to every device; older clients ignore the map. Code and tests: `packages/sync-client/src/workspace.ts` deleteFolder, readFolderTrash, restoreFolder; `do/workspace-doc.ts` restoreFolderEntry; `apps/web/src/trash/DeletedFolders.tsx`; `workspace.test.ts`, `agent-activity.test.ts`, `e2e/agent-undo.spec.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| A561  | **Agent activity: every agent change to folders, note places, settings and tags, with Undo, for 30 days (T42 review B3).** The WorkspaceDoc records each agent change to the workspace in its own SQLite (`agent_activity`), in the same call as the change, so the Worker spends no CPU and D1 no write on it: folder create, rename, move, reorder, sort and delete, the top level's sort, note moves and reorders (`note.move`, `note.reorder`, summarised by the note's title from D1), settings changes and tag renames, each with a summary and its inverse (the change that puts it back, and what it expects to find). `GET /api/agent-activity` (read scope; `?token=` for one token) lists the last 30 days newest first, at most 500; `POST /api/agent-activity/:id/undo` (write scope) applies the inverse as the person's change. Agent tokens get 403 `agent_not_allowed` for both, so an agent can neither undo another's change nor hide its own. Each part applies only if what the agent changed is still as it left it (a folder's name, parent and place, sort mode, a setting's value); otherwise 409 `changed_since` says what changed and nothing changes. Undoing a create deletes the folder (to Trash) only while it is empty and still so named; undoing a delete restores it from Trash (A560); undoing a tag rename renames back only the notes it renamed, leaving out notes that already had the new tag in a merge, and says how many kept it. Undoing twice answers `alreadyUndone`. A note's content is not listed: an agent's note edits, Trash moves and restores are versions in each note's History (A566). Note moves are not versions, so they are listed (coordinator's answer on the review, 26 Oct 2026): Undo puts the note back in its folder and place if it is still where the agent left it, and says so if it was moved, deleted or its folder is gone. Filing a note that was not in the tree (a create, a restore) is not a move. The web and Mac apps show the list in Settings → Devices and agent tokens → Agent activity, filtered by agent and kind; Android is a gap in the T40 parity matrix. | A562  | **Daily limits on what an agent token may do (T42 review B4, S5).** So that an agent in a loop, or one steered by a prompt injection, cannot do harm faster than Ryan notices it in Trash or Agent activity, each agent token may per UTC day move 100 notes to Trash, delete 25 folders, attach 50 MB of new files (a file the workspace already has costs nothing) and start 10 tag renames. Past a limit, the call is 429 `daily_limit` (`too_many_renames` for renames) with a message telling the agent to leave the rest to Ryan; a repeat that changes nothing (a note already in Trash, a folder already gone) costs nothing. People are never limited. Tag renames also have shared caps, so agents cannot spend the Free plan's 10,000 queue operations a day (about 3 per renamed note, A133): agents together rename at most 1,000 notes a day and have at most 2 of the 5 waiting renames, so Ryan's always fit. Renaming into a tag that exists merges the two, which renaming back cannot undo in notes that had both, so an agent must pass `merge: true` (409 `tag_exists` otherwise; MCP `merge`, CLI `retag --merge`). The counts live beside the activity in the WorkspaceDoc's SQLite (`agent_quota`), kept for two days. Code and tests: `do/agent-activity.ts` AGENT_LIMITS, `do/workspace-doc.ts` agentLimit, agentRenameRefusal; `agent-activity.test.ts` (limits), `cli.test.ts` (retag --merge). Anything else, including `capture.destination` and any key added to the client settings later (keyboard shortcuts, display options), is 403 `setting_not_allowed` until a decision adds it: where captures go stays the person's choice, as A346 says. | A565  | **An agent's file is decoded in the NoteDoc, up to 700 KB (T42 review B1, B2, S5).** `attach_file`, `penmoss attach` and `POST /api/notes/:id/attachments` (base64 JSON) all take files up to 700 KB, about 933 KB of base64 inside the 1 MB request limit (A153); larger is 413 `file_too_large`, and the CLI checks the size before reading the file. | A566  | **Agents move notes to Trash, never delete them for good (T42 item 10, #104).** MCP `trash_note` and `restore_note`, and the CLI's `penmoss trash` and `penmoss restore`, need the write scope; read tokens are refused (MCP lists neither tool for them). They use the NoteDoc's own Trash state, as `POST /api/notes/:id/trash` and `/restore` do: the note keeps its content and history, leaves the folder tree, and comes back for 30 days into the folder it was deleted from (the top level if that folder is gone). For an agent the NoteDoc cuts a version before and after (`Moved to Trash`, `Restored from Trash`), so History shows the change under the token's name with the ✦ chip, and Ryan's Restore undoes it. Both are idempotent: a note already in Trash answers `alreadyInTrash: true` with its recorded time and folder, and one not in Trash `restored: false`. Every other write tool answers a note in Trash with `in_trash`, whose guidance names `restore_note`. A folder-scoped token reaches only notes inside its folder (`not_found` outside), and a note it trashed has left the tree and with it the token's view: other tools answer it `not_found`, as the web's sidebar drops it. _Amended in review (Ryan's reviewer, amends A197):_ such a token may still `trash_note` it again (`alreadyInTrash: true`) and `restore_note` it when the folder recorded at deletion (`deletedFrom`) is still inside its scope; the server re-files it into that folder only, never the top level or elsewhere. A note deleted from outside or from the top level, or whose folder was deleted or moved out since, answers the same `not_found` as an unknown id (A192). REST `POST /api/notes/:id/trash` and `/restore` take the same path for agents, and an agent's restore files the note in the same request (review S4: the CLI's second request is gone), also repairing a note out of Trash but in no folder. An agent moves at most 100 notes to Trash a day (A562). `restore_version` and `revert_edit` refuse a note in Trash too (`in_trash`, review S3), and so do an agent's REST `POST /api/notes/:id/versions`, `/versions/:v/restore` and `/revert`, which `penmoss history` uses (re-review R3); the apps' History is unchanged. `DELETE /api/notes/:id` (delete for good) stays refused to every agent token. Code and tests: `agents/commands.ts` trashNote, restoreNote, trashedInScope; `do/note-doc.ts` trash, undelete; `mcp.test.ts`, `cli.test.ts` (penmoss trash), `folder-scope.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| A567  | **Agents manage folders, strictly inside a scope (T42 item 11, #104; amends A440).** Every P4 folder route (`POST /api/folders`, `PATCH /api/folders/:id`, `PATCH /api/folders/root`, `DELETE /api/folders/:id`) takes write-scope agent tokens, with the same `from` preconditions and 409s (`folder_changed`, `folder_moved`, `folder_cycle`) as devices; read tokens get 403 `insufficient_scope`. MCP gains `create_folder` (by `parentId` or `parentPath`; a same-named folder under that parent, ignoring case, is returned with `created: false`, so a retry never makes a twin), `rename_folder`, `move_folder` (also reorders with `before`/`after`), `set_folder_sort` and `delete_folder` (notes move up; the folder goes to Trash, A560, `inTrash: true`; a folder already gone is `deleted: false`; at most 25 a day, A562). An agent's folder names are trimmed and never contain `/` on every route (review N1). `POST /api/folders` takes `reuseName: true`, which returns a same-named folder under the parent instead of making a twin; the CLI's `mkdir -p` sends it, and walks from the deepest existing prefix so a token scoped to a nested folder can use it (review N5, S6). Every change an agent makes to a folder is listed in Agent activity with Undo (A561). The CLI gains `mkdir [-p]`, `rename`, `rmdir`, `sort` and `mv --folder`; `mv` of a note is unchanged. The routes, tools and CLI share `agents/folders.ts`, and each change is the WorkspaceDoc's `serverEdit` under the caller's actor. A folder-scoped token acts only on folders strictly inside its folder: its own folder can be a parent but is never renamed, moved, sorted or deleted (403 `scope_folder`); one outside reads as `folder_not_found` (and deleting it answers `deleted: false`); the top level is outside, so nothing is made or moved there and its sort order is refused (403 `outside_scope`). | A571  | **One search, always Hybrid, no type picker (T42, #104 item 2; Ryan's decision).** The Full-text / Semantic / Hybrid picker is removed, with no advanced option, and the stored choice is no longer read. Every search asks `GET /api/search?mode=hybrid`. While typing, and offline, this device's full-text index answers as before (A111); online the server's answer replaces it after a pause or on Enter. When meaning cannot answer (offline, embeddings unavailable, or the day's allowance used, A113) the results carry a quiet **Words only** chip, its reason on hover and to screen readers (`SearchOutcome.wordsOnly`); the server's hybrid notices map to it, and `notice` is left for real failures. With hybrid the only search, a note found only by meaning (≈) shows only when its best chunk is at least **0.45** cosine-similar to the query (`HYBRID_SEMANTIC_FLOOR`, bge-m3's `hybridFloor`; `fuseHybrid` in `apps/server/src/search/semantic.ts`), so "No notes match" shows when nothing is close; full-text hits keep their fused rank. Tuned with A115's 50-query eval on real embeddings (`docs/evidence/t42/eval-search.txt`): hybrid top-5 stays 50/50 and MRR 0.880, as with no floor; the labelled notes' similarity runs from 0.461 (5th lowest 0.525, median 0.623); 10 unrelated queries peak at 0.306–0.457 and keep 1 meaning hit of 500. 0.50 would cost two labelled queries (48/50, MRR 0.850). **The margin is thin and the value provisional:** the lowest labelled similarity (0.461) is 0.004 above the strongest unrelated query (0.457, "how to tune a ukulele"), on a 79-note seeded vault. After the deploy, rerun the eval, or look at the near misses, on Ryan's real notes (A12), and lower the floor if real notes found only by meaning fall under it. The floor never hides a full-text hit. The fake embedder (A105) has its own floor on its own scale, 0.2 (made-up words score at most 0.10 in the eval, the labelled median 0.30), so the e2e suite meets "No notes match" against the local Worker (review S6). Server change: needs a deploy, as MCP's hybrid default gets it too.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| A580  | ~~**The Mac signs in again as the same device (A290 for the Mac; the 25 Oct 2026 sync stop).**~~ _Superseded by D49 (T59)._ Every Mac sign-in used to make a new device. The server ties each Yjs client id to the actor that first wrote with it (A3), so a Mac that signed in again with folder or note changes not uploaded yet, or with its page still open on the old replica, had every upload of them refused (1008 “Client id belongs to another actor”), and its folder tree stopped syncing. Each Mac sign-in now sends `previousToken` on `POST /api/auth/native/token`: the current session's device token, or else the one kept from the last session signed out or refused. `SessionStore.remove` keeps the removed session, still encrypted with safeStorage (in memory only without it), as the origin's previous session in `session.json`; a new session supersedes it. Only the main process reads it: the page never sees it, and the approval page in the browser never gets it (it goes in the token exchange's body). The server already accepted this (A290): it reclaims a device of the same kind only, signed out or not, and revokes the proof. Once a sign-in replaces a session, current or previous, main signs out what is left of it: on the same device both its tokens, the page's included (a Sign out made offline left them live), on another the whole device. No server change. | A581  | **A replica the server refuses for good recovers by itself.** A close or batch error “Client id belongs to another actor” is no longer a dead end. The provider's stop says so (`clientRefused`), and `discard()` stops it writing anything more. **Folders** (`Workspace`): the server's tree is downloaded into a fresh replica (a new client id) by a provider that stores nothing; what the refused copy (the replica in memory and the stored record) would have changed is written again there field by field (`replayWorkspace`: the server's state and the refused copy merged by Yjs, then each folder, registry entry, sort mode and setting that differs set or removed, lists and objects included, compared as JSON; a key is removed only when the refused copy has nothing there); that replaces the stored record and the replica in one step, and syncs. What cannot be written again (nested Yjs types, structs whose parents never arrived) is dropped and counted, each one. One window or tab recovers at a time, under the Web Lock `penmoss-workspace-recovery`, and reads the stored record again inside it: a sibling's recovery is taken as the base, and only what this replica adds is written again (on an entry the sibling wrote again first, the fields this window edited). A restore on the server since the refusal is adopted whole instead (A5); the record is written only over the one read; edits made while it is written are replayed after the swap. A token refused while downloading signs out, and the recovery waits for the next session. A notice says what was synced again and what was dropped; one that reports drops stays until dismissed. **Notes**, open (`Notes.noteRefused`) or in catch-up sync (`adoptRefused`): the server's whole note replaces the record, and the local copy is kept apart as a conflict copy when the server's and local copies merged differ from the server's in title or content (structure, attributes and marks: a ticked task, a heading level, bold), as after a restore (A5); a copy only behind the server's is not kept. Per note under a Web Lock, the stored copy read again inside it: a second window makes no second copy, and edits made during the recovery go into the copy. Nothing is discarded before the server's copy is in hand; offline, it waits and tries again. A session recovers the folders at most three times, then stays stopped, as the pill says. Android's page holds no sync provider and its exchange already keeps refused edits apart (A290), so it needs nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | #115                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

A failure a retry clears by itself (`Unavailable`), or a note gone from the server, is not counted. | A626  | **A change made as the page goes is kept in local storage, synchronously, and merged into the stored record when the store next opens (26 Oct 2026; fixes A624's loss).** A note edit or a workspace change made less than 200 ms before a reload or a closed tab never reached IndexedDB, so offline it was gone from this device. Two causes, both shown in Chromium. The `pagehide` write (`saveNow`) read the record before writing it, and the read's callback never ran once the page was unloading: traced, the `get` was issued and no success, put, completion or abort followed. A write with no read first, in a transaction started and committed (`commit()`) inside `pagehide`, still failed 4 reloads in 30, while a local-storage write made in the same event was there every time. So `SyncProvider.saveOnUnload` hands the store's `putOnUnload` what the stored record lacks: the update since the stored state vector, or the whole document when nothing is stored yet (`UnloadWrite`). `NoteStore` keeps it in `localStorage` under `penmoss:unload:<database>:<noteId>:<page>` (a page's later write replaces its own; two pages' sit side by side). `NoteStore.open` merges every entry into its record, one at a time in one transaction, as a Yjs union, so a record another tab wrote since keeps its changes, then removes the entries it read. An entry from another epoch (A5) is never merged: a note's whole document becomes a conflict copy, the workspace's (or changes alone) are dropped. A later ordinary write that lands forgets the entry. A store that cannot keep it (no page storage, quota) falls back to `saveNow`. The web app calls it on `pagehide` and on `visibilitychange` to hidden (where it also writes as before, since hidden may be the last event on a phone), for open notes, the workspace and closed notes whose write is in flight; no `beforeunload` prompt. Shown in Chromium (the web spec, and Electron); Safari's and Firefox's local storage during `pagehide` is not tested yet. The Mac app gets it through the same web code; its main window's close and quit already wait for an ordinary save (T29), and since A640 the capture window's quit does too, and the app flushes local storage to disk as it quits. The Android editor keeps no IndexedDB copy (the app stores edits in Room), so it needs nothing. `unload-save.spec` (offline: every sync socket and request cut) types and reloads at once: it failed for both a note edit and a workspace setting before this, and passed 60 runs in 60 after.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

| A640  | **A kept change merges only into the document it was made in, and only when it adds something; each one stands alone (26 Oct 2026; review of #127).** Merging a change kept as the page went (A626) now follows these rules. One entry that throws while merging is dropped and reported, and the others still merge: before, it aborted the one transaction on every open, and entries piled up. If the merged document holds structs back for want of what they build on, the record is no longer the document the change was made in (a daily note purged and made again under its id, or a record replaced by a recovery, A581); that counts as another epoch. A change from another epoch never merges in: only a note's whole document with edits the server lacks (`unsynced`) becomes a conflict copy, as catch-up does (A269), and anything else is dropped. A note the server said is gone keeps its record as it is, `gone` and `goneCopy` included, and changes since become a conflict copy of their own: merged, its next upload would be refused as gone and copied a second time (A5). An entry the record holds already writes nothing, so a synced note stays synced. Each provider keeps its entries under its own source (its replica's client id), and a closed note's write in flight under `snapshot`, so a note's editor and an embed of it never overwrite each other's, and the snapshot is kept even while the note is open again. An entry over 1M characters is declined (the ordinary save runs), so local storage keeps room for the session token; and a session token the storage refuses leaves the page signed in with it in memory instead of failing. The capture window, closed by a quit, stores its notes first as the main window does (T29), and the app flushes local storage to disk as it quits. Failing-first tests: one per rule in the store, the provider's reload test with writes that never land after the page goes, and the web service's snapshot test.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| A660  | **A dead-lettered index event goes back to its NoteDoc (#126).** A `penmoss-note-events` message that fails all ten deliveries moves to `penmoss-note-events-dlq`, and the NoteDoc has already marked the change as sent, so the index row stayed as it was for good (a note moved to Trash still listed as live). The dead-letter queue now has a consumer (`queue/dead-letters.ts`; 25 a batch, one at a time, ten retries, no dead-letter queue of its own). It indexes nothing itself: each note a message names is handed back to its NoteDoc (`redriveIndex`), which marks the change pending again and sends a new event on the main queue after 5 minutes, four times longer each time the same change comes back, at most a day (`redriveBackoff`; a new edit starts the count over). A change already pending (a newer edit, or an earlier hand-back still backing off) is left to its own alarm. The main consumer then reads the note as it is then, so the repair is idempotent, and it stays the only writer of a note's R2 copy. The hand-back lives in Durable Object storage, not D1, so a D1 outage of any length ends in a repair. A hand-back that marks a change again is reported in Settings → Status (A263, one row a workspace, counted). A NoteDoc that cannot be reached is retried from the dead-letter queue (1 minute doubling to an hour, about 5 hours in all, within the Free plan's 24-hour retention). The sweep's check (A662) hands rows back the same way, so this one backoff governs a note that keeps failing, whichever path finds it: about six cycles on its first day and one a day after, each about 15 queue operations (a send, a read and ten retry reads, then the dead-letter write, read and ack), so about 100 on the first day and 15 a day after (of 10,000). `index.ts` routes the dead-letter queue by its exact name before the main queue's prefix. Deploy: `task queues:ensure` (run by `task deploy`) creates the dead-letter queue if missing (Cloudflare also creates it when the main consumer names it); `wrangler deploy` refuses a consumer whose queue does not exist. A consumer is not tied to a Worker version, so a rollback past this change needs `wrangler queues consumer remove penmoss-note-events-dlq penmoss`, or the old code would index dead letters directly. Code and tests: `queue/dead-letters.ts`, `do/note-doc.ts` redriveIndex, `do/note-storage.ts` indexRedriven; `index-repair.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | #126                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| A670  | **A window still on a refused folder replica after another window recovered writes nothing into the recovered record (#116; amends A581).** Each provider of the folder tree reads and writes the store through a guard (`Workspace.guardStore`) that keeps the last record it read or wrote. A stored record that no longer holds all of that at the same epoch (`replacedSince`) was replaced by another window's recovery: records otherwise only grow by merging, and a restore changes the epoch (A5). The guard then neither writes into that record nor reads it. So the lagging window's refused structs never go back into the store, and the first window is not refused again and does not recover a second time. The lagging window starts its own recovery instead (A671), which needs no server. A last-seen record that never synced (no epoch) counts as the same epoch as any stored one (#132 review N1). Such a window cannot tell a sibling's recovery from a restore by epoch, and reading the missing epoch as unknown would stop it rebasing after a sibling's recovery, which would lose its edits. The cost: if a window whose record never synced is open while another window adopts a restore (A5), it writes its own changes since onto the restored tree instead of dropping them. That needs a device whose folder tree never synced, so it is accepted. An edit the sibling already wrote again is never written a second time, so a newer edit made there since stands. A write the record already holds (one this window had from the server) is skipped. Concurrent edits resolve as Yjs resolves them: a key set in both windows keeps one value (the lagging window's, written later), and a key set in one and removed in the other keeps its value. The rebase works offline, is stored at once, replaces the replica as a recovery does, and does not count toward `MAX_RECOVERIES`. A recovery checks for it first, under the same Web Lock, and again after its download. Only the server applies it to every note, so no two clients fight over it; a lagging window's rebase applies it only to the notes it affects, inside its own write, so the server never sees those. | A680  | **A partly typed word is completed from the words as written (#120).** The full-text index holds stems, and a prefix was matched against them after stemming what was typed (as FTS5 stems a `prefix*`), so a word typed past its stem found nothing until it was finished: `happin` never reached `happi` (happiness), `conditio` `condit`, `generati` `gener`, nor `tie` `ti` (ties). Every client now keeps each note's distinct words folded but not stemmed (A681-A683). A prefix term of three characters or more (`MIN_COMPLETION_LENGTH`: porter keeps a word's first two letters, checked on every word of this log) looks up the first 64 words that start with it in code-point order (`COMPLETION_SCAN`, the order SQLite keeps them in) and keeps one word per stem that its own stem does not reach, at most 16 (`MAX_COMPLETIONS`): its completions (`completions` in `@penmoss/core/search`). Each is matched as a whole word, ORed with the prefix (`"happin"* OR "happiness"`). FTS5's bm25 scores each phrase of an OR on its own (its idf, its count) and the clients do the same, so typing part of a word finds, ranks and marks what the whole word does: `happin` and `happiness` give the same scores. The prefix's own stem still matches, so nothing found before is lost. `unfinished` (A111) counts such a word as still being typed, so semantic search leaves it out. FTS5 takes a parenthesised OR only after an explicit AND, so a MATCH with completions joins its clauses with `AND`. Only the last two prefixes of a query are completed (`MAX_COMPLETED_PREFIXES`, review S2), so a query of many `abc*` reads 128 words at most. A folder-scoped token's search is never completed (review B1): completions come from the whole workspace's words, so a word outside its scope could decide what it finds; scoped principals are agents, which search whole words. | A711  | **Windows refresh each other offline (T45; the issue's A621; extends A228).** Each window has its own sockets, so online every one hears the server. The IndexedDB store tells its page which records each committed write changed (`NoteStore.onWrite`); the page announces them, gathered for 30 ms (at most 100 ids, else "everything"): in the Mac app over IPC (`stored`), which the main process sends to every other window as `storeChanged` with the ids; in a browser over a `BroadcastChannel`, which reaches this profile's other windows and tabs. A window reads one batch at a time (`StorePuller`): the workspace when its record is named, each named open note whose socket is down (one whose socket is up hears the server, and reading the whole record on every write of another window would cost typing on a renderer the popups share), and the named notes' list entries (`getMeta`), not the whole list. The capture window's save still names nothing, so windows read everything then. A note's provider stores the first edit after 200 ms and, while typing, a write at most every 600 ms, even while the trailing text refresh (2 s) is pending; a retry after a failed write keeps its backoff. A record read from another window is stored already: the provider writes nothing for it and takes it as the record it last wrote over (`lastRev`, its state vector); each write compares the stored rev with the one its record was encoded against, so a write encoded earlier still merges what was read since, sends it on only when its socket is open, and never reads one of another epoch (it stops with an epoch mismatch, as a write would). The list re-sorts for another window's typing at most once a second, at once for a title, tag, link or Trash change. A window announces what is gathered as it closes (the Mac app, before `saved`) or its page goes (`pagehide`), and the records a store merged from unload writes as it opened go to its first listener. Only the main and note windows hear another's `stored`; the hidden capture window reads the store as it shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | #108; `window/store-sync.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
