| A723  | **Top rows drag the window; double-clicking them is native (T47; the issue's A636).** In a compact window the title-bar rows (the sidebar header, a note's or note window's top bar, the graph's bar, Settings' bar, the narrow window's app bar, the sign-in banner and Version history's head) are `-webkit-app-region: drag`, and nothing else is: there is no strip behind the page, since on a Mac a drag region wins over whatever is painted on it unless that is `no-drag`. So every control anywhere in the page (`button`, links, inputs, `label`, `summary`, focusable elements, and the roles of a control: button, link, menu items, option, tab, switch, checkbox, radio, combobox, slider, spinbutton, textbox, searchbox, treeitem) and every surface that can float over a row (Version history, menus, dialogs and overlays, scrims, the sidebar, Settings' sections list, toasts) is `no-drag`. `apps/web/src/desktop/no-drag.ts` and `styles.css` hold the same lists (a unit test compares them), and the Electron suite fails any visible control or surface in the first 48 px that is not `no-drag`, with Version history open, Settings and Trash scrolled, and menus over the top. A surface that comes before a row in the DOM and opens over it (the narrow window's drawer over the app bar, a sidebar menu over a note's top bar) stops those rows dragging while it is open, since Electron applies later regions over earlier ones and nothing relies on regions being taken in paint order; a second Electron check, without the lists, hit-tests every drag region and fails anything there that takes a click (a pointer or text cursor, a tab stop, a React handler or a DOM click listener) unless it is `no-drag` nested in the row or after it. Double-clicking a row is native: Chromium's "mac: Handle double-click-to-zoom on custom draggable regions" (2be0ae48ad7c700ec9dca07e83e73407947cbad4, 21 Apr 2026, first in Chromium 149) handles a double-click on a drag region outside the native title bar in `NativeWidgetMacNSWindow::sendEvent:` and does what `AppleActionOnDoubleClick` says (AppKit handles the native title bar's own band); Electron 45 is Chromium 156, and its `ElectronNSWindow` is a `NativeWidgetMacNSWindow` that passes events to it. So the page has no double-click handler and the main process none either; the Mac's manual check (step 15) confirms it under both "Double-click a window's title bar to" settings, and if it fails there, the follow-up is a native handler in the main process, not a page listener.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | #110; `no-drag.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

Only the apps' people do this or set a notebook's target: a token held to the agents' notebook rules, the CLI's included even with admin from a recovery code, gets 403 `notebook_not_allowed` from the confirm and mirror-target routes. A note a folder delete moved up, with no record, is held for 24 hours after the delete, or for good if the server once saw that folder flagged, so a device that turned the folder into a notebook offline can still send its records. In the gap, old apps' new notes have no record: in the default notebook they wait 24 hours (A767), in a notebook the backstop records them once settled, and the rest wait for Confirm notebook. | A771  | **Anchors are Yjs relative positions made through delta positions, the same in the editor and on the server (T48; the issue's A641).** Kept as JSON on the thread: one for a point, two for a range, the start bound to the quote's first character and the end to its last (assoc 1 and −1), so text typed at the edges stays out. The editor goes through `@y/prosemirror` 2's `resolvedPositionToDeltaPosition` and `deltaPositionToResolvedPosition` (paths in the body's tree; the binding's default transformer keeps them) and Yjs core's `createRelativePositionsFromDeltaPositions` and `createDeltaPositionsFromRelativePositions`; the server uses the same core functions, so a quote an agent anchored lights up the same text in the editor and the other way round (tested both ways). The issue named `createRelativePositionFromTypeIndex`, which cannot address text inside nested blocks. A range with nothing left between its ends, or an anchor whose block is gone, is orphaned: the thread stays, with its quote, listed after the others. The editor writes an anchor back where its own mapping and Yjs part after typing beside a thread (the binding diffs text, so typing `big ` before `garden` reused garden's `g` and moved the anchor a word early on every other device) and after a block move (a delete and a copy in Yjs; moving a block up orphaned its threads). After the editor's own undo or redo, each thread it orphaned is resolved again following the undone deletion (Yjs's `followUndoneDeletions`, used only there: only the undoing client knows where its text went back) and given a fresh anchor, so deleting a thread's text or block and undoing brings the thread back on every device, a block move's undo included. Quotes skip line symbols (T44): a thread on `★ Call the bank` quotes "Call the bank"; a point quotes its line, for context. A quote is matched in the note's visible text: a wikilink as its label (or as `[[…]]`), a hard break as a line break, and a run of blank lines as one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | #111                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Each comment pushed becomes one `notifications/claude/channel`: content the comment's author, the note's title, the quote (or a point's line) and the comment; meta `thread_id`, `note_id` and `comment_id` (identifier keys and string values only, as the channels docs require). The channel reconnects after a drop (1 s doubling to 30 s) and pings every 45 s. | A810  | ~~**A synced setting changed out of sync is held until this device has the server's state, across reloads and windows (#141, 28 Oct 2026; replaces A92's in-memory list, follows A696).**~~ _Superseded by D49 (T59)._ A change written into the WorkspaceDoc before the device has the server's state is concurrent with the server's writes of that key, and Yjs keeps the higher client id's: older history won about half the time, and A92's guard, kept in memory, went with a page reloaded or closed before its first sync (A696: 2 runs in 2). Now `Workspace.setSetting`, while the WorkspaceDoc is not `synced` (before the first sync, or offline after it), writes nothing into it: the change goes into localStorage, one item per workspace, user and setting (`penmoss.settings.unsynced/<workspace>/<user>/<key>`), with what the device had of it (its value; nothing, on a copy that has never had the server's state; or not known yet, before the stored copy is read) and the copy's epoch. Whether the copy has had the server's state is a flag of its stored record, `seeded`: the provider sets it once it applies a `sync-step2`, stores it with the record, and a merge of two records keeps it if either had it. The epoch alone is not enough: the server's opening `session` message sets and stores it before the state comes, and a change made in that gap, live or after a reload, was dropped as changed elsewhere (review of 66022b5). A record written before this has no flag: a change made before its first sync after the update goes in, as a new device's does. `settings()` lays the held changes over the WorkspaceDoc's values, so they show at once in every window and tab, which hear of each other's through `storage` events. Each is settled under a Web Lock once the copy is read, each time the WorkspaceDoc is `synced` again, and when a window in sync hears of one (the Mac's note window's, at once): A811 decides, and the change is forgotten. One made on another epoch is dropped, and a restore (`adoptRestore`) drops them all, as unsynced folder changes go (A5); signed out, they stay for that user and workspace, as the stored record does. A change made in sync is held over the value the page shows and settled at once under the same Web Lock, so a settle in another window never writes an older held change of that setting over it; held first, it is stored synchronously, so a page that goes before the lock is granted keeps it (writing only once the lock was granted lost a change saved just before a navigation). It replaces a held one. The `storage` events of one settle (one per setting) make one re-render, gathered for 50 ms. With no storage at all the changes are held in the page's memory, settled the same way, and lost if the page goes before it syncs; a page whose storage refuses a write does the same and removes the stale item. The stored data is unchanged: old clients, the server and Android read and write the same values, so nothing migrates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | #141                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A811  | **A change made elsewhere since this device last looked wins, on every client (#141).** A held change (A810) goes into the WorkspaceDoc once this device has the server's state only while the setting still has the value the device had when the change was made; then it is written after everything the server holds, so it wins on every device and never loses to older history. When the setting has another value, set elsewhere since (another device, an agent, the server), that one wins and the change is dropped: as the server takes a phone's or an agent's change (`planSettingsChange`, A410, A411), so web, Mac and Android now decide alike, and an agent's change stays undoable. A reset is a change to "not set" and follows the same rule. A device that had never had the server's state has nothing to compare with: its change goes in. A custom theme merges as the server merges one (A416, A417): the fields changed here go onto the theme as it is now, a deletion always goes, and an edit of a theme deleted since, or a new theme whose id was taken, is dropped. Nothing held is ever in the Yjs map, so no tie is decided by client id; two devices that settle at the same moment are as concurrent as two changes made while connected, which Yjs decides. Not per-key timestamps: every writer would stamp them, old clients and existing values have none, and a slow clock would lose a change silently. A held change that is dropped flips back without a notice: the setting shows the value set elsewhere, as the phone drops a row changed elsewhere (A411). A note deleted for good, at head or here, never comes back and its copy is dropped: under a new id neither the commit guard nor `reversed` would know it (the probe). A copy whose edits git already has, in or out of Trash as git has it, is dropped too. Otherwise it comes back as a new note, "<title> (recovered)", filed where the note was, and in Trash when it was in Trash: a copy, not a merge, so the old store's client ids are never written again (A850). Each copy is decided and written in one turn of the engine's lock, against the notebook as it is then, so a sync waiting ahead of it that fetches a Delete for good leaves nothing brought back; each sequence of parts has its own token. Remove counts the copies waiting and kept, says so, and offers Save their text first; Settings says when copies wait for a sync. The Mac marks a window's copy taken in only once it is, so one that failed is tried again, after a restart too. A copy the page cannot take (unreadable, too slow) is logged, kept aside in Room (`RECOVERY` rows, never sent) while the note syncs again, tried again later, and named in the notice with Save their text, which writes what of each can be read as markdown into a file the person picks. Settings and the notebook's Sync say what came back until dismissed. Each copy records its original (`recoveredFrom`, synced). One not yet pushed whose original another device deleted for good (at the fetched head) is withheld, never deleted: kept on the phone with what is typed on it (Room's `WITHHELD` rows), and Settings and Sync offer Save their text, Delete for good and Keep and sync, which main lets through for that copy once the owner check confirms it, else `purge_raced`. A purge made here leaves the copy to push; a pushed copy keeps its link; an entry never lands without its log. The Mac takes its windows' copies in under their own ids (A851), so a landed purge applies to them; there `persistent-storage` is allowed, and a window's copy it cannot read is skipped and named.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | PR #167 review S2; T50 G7, G3 (#155, #151)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

Once confirmed, the page has 120 s more to finish; past that the app says it cannot tell and to check before trying again. What the app reports is what happens. | A915  | **The Mac app stays a regular app; the capture window is a panel (T30, A720).** The capture window is an `NSPanel` (`type: 'panel'`, `captureWindowOptions`) on every Space and over full-screen apps, through `setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, {visibleOnFullScreen: true, skipTransformProcessType: true})` (`showOnEverySpace` in `apps/desktop/src/mac-window.ts`). Without `skipTransformProcessType`, Electron hides the Dock icon to float over full screen, which turns the whole app into a UIElement for as long as it runs: on macOS 26.6 (Ryan's Mac, build 335) Penmoss then had no Dock icon, `activate` left another app in front, and its menu bar drew but took no clicks. With the app regular, a plain window cannot show over a full-screen app (macOS goes back to the desktop's Space), a panel can. Every Space change goes through `mac-window.ts`, which always passes `skipTransformProcessType` (a unit test reads the sources). A capture opened while the app starts keeps its focus and closing it leaves the main window (A904) as before: the panel changes where it can show, not how the app hides or focuses its windows. AppKit logs `NSWindow does not support nonactivating panel styleMask 0x80` twice per launch, and it is harmless. Electron 45's `panel` is an `ElectronNSPanel`, a subclass of `ElectronNSWindow` and so not a real `NSPanel` (`shell/browser/ui/cocoa/electron_ns_panel.mm`). Its `styleMask` getter adds `NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel` at runtime, which is what keeps the app from activating, so every `setStyleMask` on it hands that bit to `NSWindow`, which logs it. Making the capture window sets the mask twice, both for `resizable: false`: in Electron's `SetResizable` and, most likely, in Chromium's size constraints. No window option removes the bit and keeps a panel that doesn't activate. It needs a real `NSPanel` in Electron, and Electron closed electron/electron#35815 about this log as not planned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Mac test of build 335 (T50 G3–G6), 30 Oct 2026; A720                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A920  | **Agent activity for git notebooks, read from the branch (#172; A561, A825, A858; amends A899).** What an agent changed in a git notebook's folders, note places and settings is listed with an Undo on the Mac (Settings → Git notebooks → Agent activity) and on Android (the notebook's Sync → Agent activity), offline and without a server. An agent is a writer whose `Penmoss-Writer` trailer says `agent` (a CLI or `penmoss mcp` clone added with `--agent`); each of its commits that touched the workspace logs is one entry, as each of its syncs is one version in a note's History: its change is the merged workspace at the commit against its parent's, exactly the agent's since pushes are fast-forwards and each commit writes only its own writer's log. Entries have the server's kinds, words and shapes (`GET /api/agent-activity`, `POST /api/agent-activity/:id/undo`, served by the local REST that Android's page and the CLI use), with ids from the commit's first 13 hex digits, the same on every clone, for 30 days. Undo is the server's inverse: each part only while things are as the agent left them (else 409 `changed_since`, nothing changed), all of an entry or none, tried on a copy first; it is an ordinary change by the person's writer that the next sync commits and pushes (the Mac and Android push at once), never a rewrite or a force-push. It never touches `purged`, and never files a note again that is deleted for good, in this clone's workspace or at the branch's head (#174 review): Undo skips it, says so and does the rest, as a restored folder (an agent's or a person's from Trash) skips it, so `purge_reversed` holds unchanged. An entry undone is marked in the WorkspaceDoc (`agentUndone`), so every device shows who undid it; a mark counts only when no part of the undo is still as the agent left it, read from one snapshot per list or Undo (#174 delta review). That reader rule is the protection; as defence in depth an agent's engine (`--agent`, `penmoss mcp`) never commits a mark, and main and Android's guard refuse one under an agent's trailer. An agent's writer cannot list or undo (403 `agent_not_allowed`, as an agent token on the server), its own entries included, and neither can anything the CLI or `penmoss mcp` serves, whoever's clone it is (#174 review): only the Mac's and Android's own pages undo. The server's folder Undo is refused with `changed_since`, nothing marked undone, when its folder cannot come back (its notebook deleted for good or not restored first). No owner check, as the server's Undo has none: it only puts back what an agent changed, a made folder going to Trash, unlike History's Restore and Revert, which replace a note's text and so need Touch ID or BiometricPrompt (A877, A901). Note edits, tag renames (an edit of each note in a git notebook) and Trash moves stay in each note's History, where Revert this edit undoes an agent's, as on the server (A566, A574); the CLI's help says so for `rmdir` and `retag`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | #172                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A921  | **Android signs commits with an SSH key made in the Keystore (#172; A825, A870).** Settings → Git notebooks has **Sign commits** per notebook; turning it on makes this phone's signing key first if it has none: an ECDSA P-256 key generated in the Android Keystore (`ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`), whose private half never leaves it. Generated rather than imported, so no private key ever passes through the app, a file or the clipboard. Make a new key and **Make an Ed25519 key** ask first, naming the notebooks that sign, that the old key is deleted from the phone, and to add the new public key on GitHub (#174 delta review). **Make an Ed25519 key** makes an `ssh-ed25519` key in the Keystore instead, where the device's KeyMint has Ed25519; a new key is made under a new alias and must sign and verify before it replaces the old one, so where it cannot be made the old key stays and Settings says to make a P-256 key (#174 review). Importing an existing SSH signing key is not offered: its private half would pass through the app (and the clipboard or a file) before the Keystore, OpenSSH's own key files are usually locked with bcrypt_pbkdf, which neither Android nor the JDK has, so it would take a new crypto implementation or library, and GitHub takes a signing key per device beside the others on the account; no user authentication on the key, since background syncs sign too. Settings shows the public key with Copy, to add on GitHub as a signing key, and Make a new key to replace it. Kotlin signs each commit as `git` does with `gpg.format=ssh` (an SSH signature, `PROTOCOL.sshsig`, namespace `git`, SHA-512) in the commit's `gpgsig` header, without JGit's Apache MINA signer or any new library, and checks the signature against the key before using it. It fails closed: with signing on, a commit is signed or not made, and a key that is gone or signs badly stops the sync with "Sync stopped: signing." and how to go on; nothing unsigned reaches the branch. A JVM cross-engine test drives the engine page through JGit and checks every commit with `git verify-commit` and `ssh-keygen -Y verify`. The Mac and the CLI sign as git's configuration says, as before.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | #172                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| A997  | **`GitHubTransport`: a git notebook over GitHub's REST API (T55).** `@penmoss/git-notebook/github` implements `GitTransport` with the Git Data API: the branch's ref for `fetch` (409, an kept by id), new blobs, a tree on the head's tree and a commit for `commit` (null when the tree would not change; removing an absent path is skipped), and a ref update without force for `push`: fewer than 300 files; otherwise null, and the engine compares trees. `log` reads the commits API (at most 1,000 without a limit) and `readAt` an old commit's tree. CI's mac-release job puts a signed build's zip, dmg and feed there, the feed last, and keeps the newest 5 builds (`mac/builds.txt`); until the `PENMOSS_DOWNLOADS_R2_TOKEN` secret (a Cloudflare token that can edit that bucket's objects) is set it warns and skips. The app's feed is electron-updater's generic provider at that URL, with no token. Check Now and Penmoss → Check for Updates… check either way. A newer build is only offered (the status line, and a notice in the notes' window); Install and Restart downloads it, shows the progress and restarts into it. The switch and Install and Restart need a click or key press; unsigned builds never check. The GitHub token is now for Send feedback alone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Tests: desktop `updater.test.ts`, `shell.test.ts`; | A1151 | **The model comes once from Hugging Face, pinned (D59).** A manifest in `@penmoss/embed` names the repository, the commit and each file's size and SHA-256. It goes into a temporary folder renamed to `~/.penmoss/models/<model>@<revision>/`, so two downloaders never leave half a model. In the app it runs in an Electron `utilityProcess`, four threads; in the CLI and the MCP server, in the app binary's own process. The page keeps its CSP: a page worker would get only one thread without cross-origin isolation (T70: 430 ms a chunk, against 173–474 ms in the utility process on four threads). The packaged build is checked to hold no `.node` file. esbuild bundles the runtime's ESM Node build, so `import.meta.url` is defined from `__filename`. The runtime fixes its thread count on first use in a process. The page reaches the app's service only through main's named calls (`penmossDesktop.meaning`: status, update, close, search, setEnabled), which main checks and relays over the utility process's own port; no port is handed to the page, so the preload stays a few named calls (T76). Main restarts a crashed service after 1, 5, 30, then 120 s; each start has a new `generation`, and the page sends its notes again (versions first, then the sections the service asks for). | A1179 | **Keys typed straight after New Note land in the note; an early Enter in the title waits for the body (7 Nov 2026).** `unload-save.spec` failed now and then in CI with an empty note: ⌘⌥N pressed as the page showed made the note, but its view came 20–90 ms later, and the keys typed meanwhile went to `<body>`. Traced in the page, two causes. useSyncExternalStore subscribes in a passive effect, which React runs in a later task, and Chromium handles queued keys first: a `navigate` before that task reached React only when the task ran. And `navigate` told its listeners through a DOM event, so while they ran `window.event` was that event, not the key, and React gave their updates the default priority (a later task) instead of the key's (the microtask after it). `useLocation` now also listens from the commit (a layout effect, as the command dispatcher does, A697), and `navigate` calls its listeners directly: the note view commits, and its title takes focus, before the next key. Separately, Enter in the title before the editor existed was dropped, and what followed stayed in the title: it is now queued, and when the body opens the text typed after it moves to the body's start (the title keeps it when it changed any other way). `new-note-typing.spec` types at once after the shortcut with the CPU throttled 6×: 9 failures in 40 before, 0 in 40 after; its second test reads the store slowly so the body opens late: 10 of 10 failed before, 10 of 10 pass. A web unit test navigates from a key after the commit and before passive effects. The flaky spec types without waiting for the title's focus again, and pushes its set-up by Sync Now (A1013) instead of waiting out the push delay twice in its 30 s. Not covered: a shortcut the Mac app's menu takes arrives as an IPC message, not a key, so what it changes still renders at the default priority (not seen failing in a test).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| A1183 | **Fork pull requests never run on the self-hosted runners (P10 of the public release plan, #237, T80.2 #285; amends A405's view of `if:` and A702).** Every job on a self-hosted runner, in a workflow that runs on `pull_request`, starts its `if:` with `(github.event_name != 'pull_request' \|\| github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) && …`; `pick`, `check`, `e2e`, `budgets` and `android` would otherwise run a fork's pull request on Ryan's Macs once the repository is public. No workflow uses `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`, and every workflow's default permissions are `contents: read`. `.github/scripts/workflow-guard.mjs` reads the workflows line by line (they are Prettier-formatted, so no YAML parser is added) and `task workflows:test`, part of `task check`, fails on any job without the guard. Every job of a fork's pull request is skipped, and GitHub counts a skipped required check as passing (A1181), so a fork's pull request is never merged as it is; it merges only through a maintainer's branch. A fork's own copy of the workflows can drop the guard, so the boundary is the setting: on going public Ryan sets fork pull request approval to all external contributors, and nobody approves a fork's run; a maintainer reads the change and pushes it to a branch here instead (`docs/ci.md` §9). (1) A bare **publish repo**, `<stateDir>/publish`, that no sandbox mounts, with config the host writes (origin, identity). The host fetches main from GitHub into it. To read or publish a run it fetches the run's branch _from_ the clone (`git fetch <clone> +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/factory/<run>`; git's upload-pack is meant to be safe against an untrusted repository), and diffs, counts commits, checks whether the branch is behind main, reads main's decisions and the pushed head there. A push is refused unless the branch descends from the main the host fetched before the gate's rebase, then goes from the publish repo with the explicit lease (A1228) and the app's token. A new publish repo fetches every branch first, so the leases start from GitHub, as a fresh clone did. (3) **Every host git call goes through `tools/factory/src/git.ts`:** `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, and `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c credential.helper= -c protocol.file.allow=user -c submodule.recurse=false`, with the token helper only for the push and its `ls-remote`. None runs with `-C` or a working folder in the clone or a worktree. Sandcastle's own worktree commands stay its own (it hardens them itself). (4) **The janitor runs no git:** it lists the factory's worktrees folder (`<clone>/.sandcastle/worktrees`) itself, deletes only real folders directly in it, never a path `git worktree list` names, and drops the clone's records of worktrees that are gone, as `git worktree prune` does. (5) **The Mac proof runs the factory's own `scripts/vm/desktop-test.sh`** (its code checkout, A1226), not the worktree's, which an agent can edit, and names the worktree in `PENMOSS_VM_ROOT`, which the script takes as the checkout to copy into the VM. The tests plant only URL rewrites and push URLs that point at a decoy repository (in the clone's config and through `commondir`), never anything that runs. | A1232 | **The factory numbers only the decisions a branch added, and every sandbox of a run starts from the main the host fetched (PEN-75's run, 8 Nov 2026; amends A1228 and A1230).** (1) **Numbering.** After the gate's rebase the host fetches the branch into the publish repo and reads `git diff -U0 <base>...<branch>` there, `<base>` being the main the host recorded for the run. Only a `\| A-NEW-k \|` row among the lines the branch added to `docs/decisions.md` defines a placeholder. Each defined key gets the next number (after `main`'s highest and the `decision-numbers` reservation, as before) on the lines the branch added: its row, and any other added line that names it, outside `tools/factory/` (whose code and tests name placeholders as data). A placeholder in text the branch didn't add (the instructions in AGENTS.md, the prompts and `docs/factory.md`) stays as it is, and so does one the branch never defined. No defined key: no commit, and nothing reserved. The host writes only regular files inside the worktree, never through a symlink. Why: numbering grepped whole files for `A-NEW-n`, so PEN-75's run, which recorded no decision, rewrote the two example placeholders in AGENTS.md's instruction on numbering new decisions to `A1232` and `A1233`, committed that and reserved both numbers. (2) **The run's start.** The first command in every sandbox the host opens (`sandboxStartCommand`, `tools/factory/src/host.ts`) fetches main into the runs' clone with the sandbox's read-only token, puts the clone's `origin/main` at the run's base (the main the host fetched into the publish repo; a run fetches it there before its first sandbox), and fast-forwards the branch onto that base when the branch has no commits of its own, as a new branch, which Sandcastle makes from the clone's `origin/main`, has none. A branch with commits of its own (a restarted run's, R12, or a fix or review round's) stays where it is, and the gate rebases it. When the fetch fails, the sandbox is closed and the run stops with the reason. Why: after A1230 the host never runs git in the clone, and only the gate sandbox moved its main, so a new run started from wherever the last gate had left it: PEN-75's started from a main older than a fix merged before the run began.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| A1233 | **The Factory UI is two views over one view model, Inbox and Pipeline, and Needs you lists only the factory's own claims (Ryan's pick on the redesign canvas, 8 Nov 2026; amends F20 and F21's page, not their writes).** `ui/model.ts` builds one view and `ui/page.html` draws it twice, switched in a shared header: **Inbox** (what needs Ryan, oldest first, each with what to do: answer the plan, review the PR, unblock, fix the Mac, fix the card; then Working, the queue and the slots' runs over 12 hours, with the detail beside the list) and **Pipeline** (a row per card, a column per step, Todo · Plan · Build · Gate · Proof · PR + CI · Review · Merge · Done, and a marker on the card's step coloured by who has the turn). Both use the same header, detail, chips and step marker; a row or a timeline bar opens the same detail; the address is `#inbox`, `#pipeline` or either with `/issue-<n>`, and a notification's `#issue-<n>` opens on that card, one column at phone width. (1) **Whose cards.** Todo and Planning cards are the factory's by status; In Progress, In Review and Done cards only when `runs.jsonl` holds their `claimed` line. The rest are counted, not listed. Needs you is built from what the factory recorded: the last run's stop (a `blocked` reason or a `failed` error), the plan's open points (`askedAt`), a live run's `waitingFor`, a PR in review, or labels the factory won't start; a Blocked card with no stop of the factory's is paused by Ryan and waits in the queue. (2) **Words, not events.** A `failed` run that never reached `agent-finished` and either never logged `agent-started` or failed with exit 127 says "Failed before the agent started: <error>", with the error cut to its last line (`claude: command not found (exit 127)`) and, for a machine error, the command that fixes it; agent rounds count from 1. (3) **Health.** From `status.json` and `kill -0` on its pid: Running, Paused for an update, Not polling (alive, no poll for three intervals), Not running (the pid has exited) and No status; when it isn't fresh the page says so with the command and dims the rest, and a dead daemon's `running` list is ignored, so nothing shows as live. It also names a wrong checkout (A1226) and a failing doctor check, from `doctor/summary-slot<n>.json`, which a full `factory:doctor` now writes. (4) A Done card counts by its last ledger line when there's no `done` line, since the merge step logs to the daemon's log, not the ledger. Unchanged: the token cookie, the `Host` and `Origin` checks, `POST /action` only with the page's Origin and only through Ryan's own key, and the daemon's prompts read only Ryan's words as instructions. Left out: **Pause / Resume new work** (the only hold, `update.pause`, belongs to a live `factory:update` pid, so a pause of Ryan's needs a new daemon input, not a page change) and **Reveal the run folder** (it would make the server run `open`; the detail shows the path with a Copy button). Why: the old page put every card with a reason in Waiting on you, so it listed In Progress cards the factory never claimed (PEN-30's tasks), said "Paused: Agent working (round 0)" for PEN-75's run that failed before the agent started, and showed a dead daemon's last status as live.                                                                                                                        |

| A1236 | **`factory:update` restarts the daemon and the UI cleanly (PEN-75's run, 8 Nov 2026; amends A1226 and A1230).** (1) **Only the daemon prepares the runs' clone.** Both LaunchAgents ran `openFactory`, which ran `ensureClone`, which wrote the clone's config with `git config --file`; restarted together by `factory:update`, the UI and the daemon wrote it at once, and the daemon lost `config.lock` and exited 1. The UI now opens the factory with `{ clone: false }` (it reads the tracker and the state folder only), and every config write of the clone and the publish repo (`ensureConfig`, `tools/factory/src/git.ts`) reads the key first and writes only a value that differs, so a second start (the daemon after an update, a foreground `factory run`) takes no lock. (2) **A daemon that exits on an error comes back.** Both plists already had `KeepAlive` `{ SuccessfulExit: false }` and `ThrottleInterval` 30, so launchd relaunches an exit 1 or 2 within 30 s of its start, and a clean stop (SIGTERM, exit 0, `factory:stop`'s bootout) stays stopped; PEN-75's `- 1` in `launchctl list` was that throttle. A test now holds both plists to it (`test/code.test.ts`). (3) **Loading the LaunchAgents again survives launchd's lag.** `launchctl bootout` returns before launchd has removed the service, and a `bootstrap` then fails with "5: Input/output error", which left both agents down after PEN-75's third update. `factory:install` and `factory:update` now wait (at most 10 s) until `launchctl print` no longer finds each label, and a failed bootstrap boots the label out again, waits until it is gone and tries again, four times in all. Each agent is tried even when the other failed, and the error names which. `task factory:start` (`factory start`) starts both, not only the daemon: it loads one that is booted out, the same way, kickstarts one that is loaded but not running (without `-k`, so a running one is left alone), and says to run `factory:install` when a plist is missing. (4) **An update ends with the new daemon's status.** After the restart `factory:update` waits, for at most two poll intervals and a minute, for a `status.json` written after the restart by a pid that is running, and prints it as `factory:status` does; without one it says so and exits 1. `factory:status` says when the pid in `status.json` isn't running, so an old daemon's last poll no longer reads as the live one's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| A1283 | **A picture leaves no empty line under it (PEN-66, 10 Nov 2026; amends A506, replaces A1107's lone-picture rule).** A picture was a block (A506), so when it ended its paragraph or list item, ProseMirror's cursor helpers after it (a separator and a trailing break) made an empty line under it, 1.7 em tall, that could not be deleted; A1107 fixed only a paragraph holding exactly one picture. Now the node (`.pm-image`) is inline and holds a frame (`.pm-image-frame`: the picture or its placeholder, the resize handle, the fields), an inline box the picture's own size, in paragraphs, list items, quotes, table cells and headings, linked, bold or highlighted. The helpers after a picture that ends its block share its line. The frame is a grid with the picture, handle and fields in one cell, never positioned except while its fields show: beside a positioned box in the node (as A1107's `position: relative` picture was) Chromium and Electron draw no caret after the picture, by End or by a click right of it. The caret there is drawn at the picture's right edge, 3 px of padding clear of it, as tall as the picture (Chromium's caret beside an inline box); a highlighted picture that ends its block shows those 3 px. That collapsed selection has no `getClientRects()` in Chromium, so the specs find the drawn caret by its pixels. Text keeps off that line (A506 stays): before the picture its `::before`, a block 0.4 em tall, breaks the line, unless the picture already starts its line (after a separator: first in its block, or after a line break) and 0 tall under another picture, so stacked pictures touch; after it the frame's end margin, as wide as the line, wraps what follows, unless the picture ends its block (a soft line break after it already breaks the line, with no empty one). The separator before such a picture is taken out of the line (`position: absolute`), or Chromium breaks the line between them. So a block that ends in a picture ends at its bottom edge, and the next block is its normal gap below (0.85 em, 0.15 em between list items); a picture alone in its block is as tall as the block. Each rule looks only at the picture's neighbours. Chosen over a frame as wide as the line (the first try), which drew the caret and a highlight across the whole line. A highlight that runs on past the picture still colours its line's end. Markdown untouched (rendering only); Android shares the stylesheet. Tests: `apps/web/test/e2e/picture-gap.spec.ts`, `apps/desktop/test/e2e/picture-gap.spec.ts`, `PictureGapInstrumentedTest`, `writing.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

The same `--settings` deny `AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode` and `ExitPlanMode` and set `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, so nothing waits on a keypress. The runner drops `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from Claude's environment and seeds `$HOME/.claude` (the sandbox's own home) with onboarding, trust and the login's account. The login is a second claude.ai login, separate from Ryan's (`agents.claude.login`, `~/.config/penmoss-factory/claude`, made once with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=… claude auth login`); Claude Code keeps it in the keychain item `Claude Code-credentials-<sha256(dir)[0:8]>`. Only the host holds its refresh token. Before each session the host refreshes it when its access token has under 4 h left (`claude auth login` with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`, Claude Code's own refresh; one at a time, since a refresh token works once), then stages the access token alone, with the account, in `<state>/claude-login/slot<n>` (mode 700, mounted read-only into that slot only) and deletes it when the session ends. The link is posted on the card and shown in the Factory UI ("Open in Claude", from `runs/<id>/chat-url` while the session runs). With no login, or one that can't be refreshed, the session runs on the setup token with no chat, and the run log says why. `task factory:doctor` reports the login and warns in its last 7 days. Proven inside the slot's Seatbelt sandbox before it shipped (PEN-103).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Ryan asked for Remote Control on every session. Only a stored full-scope login opens it; staging the short-lived access token alone keeps the refresh token on the host, and the agent can already read the sandbox's own secrets, so the exposure is about 8 h of that one login.                |
| A1288 | **Every Claude Code session the factory starts is named with a `[PF] ` prefix (11 Nov 2026; amends A1281, A1286, A1287).** Planning sessions are `[PF] Penmoss PEN-n plan` and a run's agent sessions `[PF] Penmoss PEN-n run`, for both `--name` and `--remote-control`. A session started before this, named without the prefix, is still recognised as its card's (`sessionIssue`), so a planning session that is running when the factory updates keeps its card. | A1289 | **A run's sandbox is ready before its agent starts, and the agent checks only what it changed (11 Nov 2026).** Past runs' logs showed the same false starts again and again. After the sandbox starts from main, the host runs `SANDBOX_READY` in it (host.ts): `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline` from the factory's pnpm store (about 5 s; four runs had begun on missing modules or `task setup`), and a `$HOME/.zshenv` that every zsh reads, the shell the agents' Bash tools run: `TMPPREFIX=$TMPDIR/zsh`, since zsh writes here-documents to `/tmp`, outside the sandbox (17 agent heredocs had failed), and `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` with Java's temp folder and home in the sandbox, which agents had to remember to export before Gradle (KSP, Robolectric, the debug keystore). A failed install is logged and the run goes on. The build prompt says the sandbox is ready and that `/tmp` can't be written, and asks the agent for `task check:changed -- origin/main` and the e2e specs that cover its change instead of the whole `task check`, which the gate runs right after it anyway (agents had run it 42 times, 169 minutes in all). whole check, so nothing is checked less.                                                                                                                                                                |
| A1292 | **The gate's rebase replays the factory's own numbering commit (11 Nov 2026; amends A1250).** PEN-71's gate rebase stopped on "Number the new decisions: A-NEW-1 is A1290" after #131 and #132 added rows to main: that commit edits the branch's `A-NEW-1` row right where main's new rows are, so the merge base isn't empty and neither the append merge nor the unpadded merge applies, and the agent spent a round rebasing by hand. When a rebase stops on a commit whose subject is the numbering message, `rebaseOntoMain` takes the rebased table so far, gives the numbers named in the subject to the rows main doesn't have (`newRows`), formats it and continues; a number main has taken meanwhile is moved on afterwards as before (A1228). Any other conflict still goes to the agent.
